inhNote.MatSiblingsShare: Maternal half-siblings share one third equally, male and female alike.
inhNote.Umariyya: This is one of the two 'Umariyyah cases: the mother takes a third of what remains after the spouse's share.
inhNote.GrandmothersShare: The two grandmothers share one sixth.
inhNote.FullSistersGhayr: Full sisters become residuaries together with the daughters.
inhNote.Akdariyya: This is the Akdariyyah case: the sister is given a half and the grandfather a sixth, raising the case to 9; their shares are then pooled and split two to one, giving 27.
inhNote.JaddRule: With siblings, the grandfather takes whichever is best for him: sharing, or a third of the estate — the majority view (Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali). Abu Hanifa held that the grandfather excludes the siblings like the father.
inhNote.JaddRuleOtherFard: With siblings, the grandfather takes whichever is best for him: sharing, or a third of the remainder, or a sixth of the estate — the majority view (Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali). Abu Hanifa held that the grandfather excludes the siblings like the father.
inhNote.Muadda: Paternal half-siblings were counted against the grandfather (mu'addah), then their share returns to the full siblings where needed.
inhNote.NothingLeft: Nothing remains after the fixed shares, so the residuary heir ({winner}) receives nothing.
inhNote.Mushtaraka: This is the Mushtarakah (Himariyyah) case: Malikis and Shafi'is let the full siblings share the third with the maternal siblings; the result here follows the Hanafi and Hanbali view.
inhNote.Awl: The fixed shares exceeded the base, so the case was raised from {asl} to {awl} ('awl) and every share shrinks in proportion.
inhNote.Radd: There is no residuary heir, so the surplus is returned to the sharers in proportion to their shares, except the spouses.
inhNote.SpouseOnlyRadd: The only heir is the spouse: many contemporary scholars and several family laws return the remainder to them; earlier scholars gave it to distant kindred, then the public treasury.
inhNote.NoHeirs: There is no sharer or residuary heir; the estate goes to distant kindred, then the public treasury. Refer to the competent court.

onboarding: Muslim tools in one app: prayer, qibla, Quran, zakat and inheritance. No ads, and most of it works offline.
Accurate times for your city with adhan alerts, the qibla by compass, and the Hijri date and Islamic events.
Mushaf pages, tafsir and recitation, focus and memorization modes, and a daily khatma that tracks your progress and streak.
Zakat in its five types, inheritance and expiations — every ruling comes with its evidence from the Quran, the Sunnah and the scholars.
Use the search bar on Home for tools, cities, surahs, ayahs and adhkar, in any language. You can replay this tour from Settings.
strings.privacyText: The app collects no personal data and uses the internet only to download the tafsirs you choose and to play recitations when you ask. Your location is used only on your device to compute prayer times and the qibla, and your settings and numbers stay on your device.
strings.qiblaTip: To change your location, use the Prayer Times page. Hold the phone flat and away from metal for an accurate reading.

evidence.Allah commanded His Prophet ﷺ to take ch: Allah commanded His Prophet ﷺ to take charity from people's wealth to purify them; it is the third pillar of Islam.
evidence.The warning against hoarding gold and si: The warning against hoarding gold and silver
evidence.Whoever hoards gold and silver without p: Whoever hoards gold and silver without paying their zakat is warned of punishment, so zakat is due on gold, silver and money.
evidence.Five awaq are 200 dirhams, about 595 g o: Five awaq are 200 dirhams, about 595 g of pure silver.
evidence.Gold nisab, the lunar year and the rate: Gold nisab, the lunar year and the rate
evidence.Twenty dinars are about 85 g of pure gol: Twenty dinars are about 85 g of pure gold. Zakat is due only after a full lunar year, and the rate is one fortieth (2.5%).
evidence.Abu Dawud (1573), graded authentic by al: Abu Dawud (1573), graded authentic by al-Albani
evidence.Scholars agree that the zakat of gold, s: Scholars agree that the zakat of gold, silver and money is one fortieth once it reaches the nisab and a year has passed.
evidence.Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Ijma'; Ibn Qudamah, a: Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Ijma'; Ibn Qudamah, al-Mughni
evidence.The Hanafis require zakat on it, as did: The Hanafis require zakat on it, as did Ibn Baz and Ibn Uthaymin among contemporaries; most Malikis, Shafi'is and Hanbalis exempt permissible jewellery kept for wear. The app lets you choose.
evidence.Ibn Qudamah, al-Mughni; Fatawa Ibn Baz: Ibn Qudamah, al-Mughni; Fatawa Ibn Baz
evidence.Debts you owe that are due now are deduc: Debts you owe that are due now are deducted from your wealth according to the Hanafis and Hanbalis, which the app follows; the later Shafi'i view does not deduct them.
evidence.Zakat on goods held for sale: Zakat on goods held for sale
evidence.Its chain is debated, but the Companions: Its chain is debated, but the Companions such as Umar and Ibn Umar acted on it, and all four schools hold zakat due on trade goods.
evidence.Valued at market price at the end of the: Valued at market price at the end of the year
evidence.Trade goods are added to your money for: Trade goods are added to your money for the nisab, and one fortieth of their value on the day zakat falls due is paid.
evidence.Shares bought for trading are valued at: Shares bought for trading are valued at market price like trade goods; long-term shares owe zakat on their portion of the company's zakatable assets, as decided by the International Islamic Fiqh Academy.
evidence.The letter Abu Bakr wrote for Anas when: The letter Abu Bakr wrote for Anas when sending him to Bahrain, giving the full schedule for camels and sheep; the app calculates by it.
evidence.Nothing is due below thirty; for every t: Nothing is due below thirty; for every thirty a one-year calf, and for every forty a two-year cow.
evidence.They must graze on open pasture most of: They must graze on open pasture most of the year, per the majority, so stall-fed and working animals owe nothing; the Malikis require it on these too. Animals held for sale are valued as trade goods.
evidence.Ibn Qudamah, al-Mughni; Ibn Rushd, Biday: Ibn Qudamah, al-Mughni; Ibn Rushd, Bidayat al-Mujtahid
evidence.The herd must be owned at nisab for a fu: The herd must be owned at nisab for a full lunar year; their young are counted with them.
evidence.Bint makhad: a she-camel of one year; bi: Bint makhad: a she-camel of one year; bint labun: two; hiqqah: three; jadha'ah: four. Tabi' (cattle): one year; musinnah: two. Shah: a sheep of six months or a goat of one year.
evidence.The zakat of crops and fruit is due at h: The zakat of crops and fruit is due at harvest; no year needs to pass.
evidence.A tenth (10%) when watered without cost,: A tenth (10%) when watered without cost, by rain or springs; half a tenth (5%) when watered at cost; three quarters of a tenth (7.5%) when half and half.
evidence.Five awsuq are 300 sa', estimated at abo: Five awsuq are 300 sa', estimated at about 612 kg of wheat; it varies slightly by crop.
evidence.For the majority: grains and fruit that: For the majority: grains and fruit that are measured and stored, such as wheat, barley, rice, dates and raisins; Abu Hanifa required it on all produce of the land.
evidence.Rikaz is treasure buried before Islam; a: Rikaz is treasure buried before Islam; a fifth (20%) is due immediately.
evidence.No nisab or year for rikaz: No nisab or year for rikaz
evidence.The majority take a fifth of any amount: The majority take a fifth of any amount without waiting a year; the Shafi'is require the nisab.
evidence.Hanbalis: one fortieth on any mineral wo: Hanbalis: one fortieth on any mineral worth the gold nisab; Malikis and Shafi'is limit it to gold and silver; Hanafis treat it like rikaz (a fifth). The app uses one fortieth.
evidence.Ibn Qudamah, al-Mughni; al-Kasani, Bada': Ibn Qudamah, al-Mughni; al-Kasani, Bada'i' al-Sana'i'
evidence.It is due for every Muslim and those he: It is due for every Muslim and those he supports: one sa' of the local staple food, before the Eid prayer.
evidence.Pay it on the eve of Eid or a day or two: Pay it on the eve of Eid or a day or two before; do not delay it past the Eid prayer.
evidence.Abu Dawud (1609), graded hasan by al-Alb: Abu Dawud (1609), graded hasan by al-Albani
evidence.The majority require food; the Hanafis a: The majority require food; the Hanafis allow its value in money. A sa' is about 2.04 kg of wheat; for rice 2.5–3 kg is taken as a precaution.
evidence.Ibn Qudamah, al-Mughni; Permanent Commit: Ibn Qudamah, al-Mughni; Permanent Committee fatwas
evidence.Feeding a poor person as fidya: Feeding a poor person as fidya
evidence.Ibn Abbas said it is for the elderly man: Ibn Abbas said it is for the elderly man and woman who cannot fast: for each day they feed a poor person.
evidence.One mudd (about 0.75 kg) per poor person: One mudd (about 0.75 kg) per poor person for the Malikis, Shafi'is and Hanbalis; half a sa' for the Hanafis. The app lets you choose.
evidence.Feed ten poor people with the average fo: Feed ten poor people with the average food of your household, or clothe them, or free a slave; whoever cannot, fasts three days.
evidence.Expiation for intercourse during a Ramad: Expiation for intercourse during a Ramadan day
evidence.In order: free a slave; if not possible,: In order: free a slave; if not possible, fast two consecutive months; if unable, feed sixty poor people — and make up the day.
evidence.1) From the estate, pay the funeral cost: 1) From the estate, pay the funeral costs, then debts, then any bequest to a non-heir up to one third. 2) Give those with fixed shares their Quranic portions: a half, a quarter, an eighth, two thirds, a third and a sixth. 3) What remains goes to the agnatic heirs ('asabah), nearest first. 4) Nearer relatives exclude more distant ones. 5) If the shares exceed the estate, all are reduced in proportion ('awl); if something is left and there is no 'asabah, it returns to the sharers other than the spouses (radd).
evidence.The verse of children and parents: The verse of children and parents
evidence.Children: a son receives twice a daughte: Children: a son receives twice a daughter's share. One daughter alone takes a half, two or more take two thirds. Father and mother: each takes a sixth if the deceased has children. If there are no children and the parents inherit, the mother takes a third and the father the rest; if the deceased has siblings (two or more), the mother takes a sixth. All of this is after any bequest and debt.
evidence.The verse of spouses and maternal siblin: The verse of spouses and maternal siblings
evidence.Husband: a half if the wife has no child: Husband: a half if the wife has no children, a quarter if she has. Wife: a quarter if the husband has no children, an eighth if he has; several wives share it. Maternal siblings in kalalah: one takes a sixth, two or more share a third equally, males and females alike.
evidence.The kalalah verse: full and paternal sib: The kalalah verse: full and paternal siblings
evidence.When the deceased leaves no child and no: When the deceased leaves no child and no father: one sister takes a half, two or more take two thirds; if they are brothers and sisters together, a male takes twice a female's share; a brother inherits all of his sister's estate if she has no child.
evidence.The remainder goes to the nearest male a: The remainder goes to the nearest male agnate
evidence.After the fixed shares, the nearest agna: After the fixed shares, the nearest agnate takes the rest: the son, then the son's son, then the father, then the grandfather, then brothers and their sons, then paternal uncles and their sons.
evidence.A son's daughter with a daughter; sister: A son's daughter with a daughter; sisters with daughters
evidence.A son's daughter with one daughter takes: A son's daughter with one daughter takes a sixth to complete two thirds, and full or paternal sisters with daughters become residuaries and take the remainder.
evidence.The Prophet ﷺ gave the grandmother a six: The Prophet ﷺ gave the grandmother a sixth, as al-Mughirah and Muhammad ibn Maslamah testified (Abu Dawud 2894), and there is consensus on it when there is no mother. The paternal grandfather takes the father's place when there is no father; scholars differ on the grandfather with siblings.
evidence.Bequests are limited to a third: Bequests are limited to a third
evidence.A bequest may not exceed a third of the: A bequest may not exceed a third of the estate unless the heirs consent, and there is no bequest to an heir (Abu Dawud 2870, al-Tirmidhi 2120).
evidence.There is no inheritance between people o: There is no inheritance between people of different religions, and neither a deliberate killer nor a slave inherits.
evidence.The school followed in the calculation: The school followed in the calculation
evidence.The app follows the majority on exclusio: The app follows the majority on exclusion, 'awl, radd and the 'Umariyyatan, and notes disputed cases such as the grandfather with siblings and al-Mushtarakah. For large or complex estates, consult a Sharia court or a qualified scholar.
evidence.Allah made the prayers obligatory at kno: Allah made the prayers obligatory at known times; they are not prayed before them nor delayed past them without an excuse.
evidence.From the sun's decline to the night, and: From the sun's decline to the night, and the dawn
evidence.The verse gathers the five times: Dhuhr: The verse gathers the five times: Dhuhr and Asr from the sun's decline, Maghrib and Isha until the dark of night, and the recitation at dawn.
evidence.The times are calculated from it: the su: The times are calculated from it: the sun's zenith for Dhuhr, an object's shadow for Asr, sunset for Maghrib, the disappearance of twilight for Isha, and true dawn for Fajr.
evidence.Asr begins, for the majority, when an ob: Asr begins, for the majority, when an object's shadow equals its length, and for the Hanafis when it is twice its length. Organizations differ on the sun's depression for Fajr and Isha (Muslim World League 18° and 17°, Umm al-Qura 18.5° and Isha 90 minutes after Maghrib), so the app lets you choose the method used in your country.
evidence.Facing the qibla is a condition of the p: Facing the qibla is a condition of the prayer, and the qibla is the Ka'bah in Makkah.
evidence.Facing the direction is enough when far: Facing the direction is enough when far away
evidence.The Prophet ﷺ said it to the people of M: The Prophet ﷺ said it to the people of Madinah, and the majority hold that whoever cannot see the Ka'bah need only face its direction by his best effort; a slight deviation does no harm.
evidence.Al-Tirmidhi (342) and Ibn Majah (1011),: Al-Tirmidhi (342) and Ibn Majah (1011), graded authentic
evidence.How the app finds the direction: How the app finds the direction
evidence.It calculates the shortest path over the: It calculates the shortest path over the earth's surface (the great circle) from your location to the Ka'bah, the approach used by astronomical and religious bodies. Keep the phone away from metal and magnets for an accurate compass.
evidence.Allah made the new moons a measure of ti: Allah made the new moons a measure of time for people's worship and dealings, such as fasting, Hajj and the waiting period.
evidence.Twelve months, four of them sacred: Twelve months, four of them sacred
evidence.The number of months with Allah is twelv: The number of months with Allah is twelve, among them the sacred months: Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, Muharram and Rajab.
evidence.The month begins with the sighting: The month begins with the sighting
evidence.Ramadan and the two Eids begin with the: Ramadan and the two Eids begin with the sighting of the crescent, or by completing thirty days.
evidence.The calculated calendar and the sighting: The calculated calendar and the sighting
evidence.The app shows the calculated Umm al-Qura: The app shows the calculated Umm al-Qura calendar, suitable for general dates. For the start of Ramadan and the Eids, follow the announcement of the religious authority in your country, which may differ by a day.
evidence.Resolutions of the Islamic Fiqh Academy: Resolutions of the Islamic Fiqh Academy
evidence.Allah made fasting it obligatory, and in: Allah made fasting it obligatory, and in it the Quran was revealed.
evidence.Better than a thousand months; seek it i: Better than a thousand months; seek it in the odd nights of the last ten of Ramadan, as in Bukhari (2017).
evidence.Fasting the day of Arafah is recommended: Fasting the day of Arafah is recommended for those not on Hajj, and Ashura on the 10th of Muharram, preferably with the 9th.
evidence.Muslims have two Eids: al-Fitr on the 1s: Muslims have two Eids: al-Fitr on the 1st of Shawwal and al-Adha on the 10th of Dhu al-Hijjah.
evidence.Allah commands the believers to remember: Allah commands the believers to remember Him often and glorify Him morning and evening.
evidence.The tasbih counter's presets follow it:: The tasbih counter's presets follow it: 33 tasbih, 33 tahmid, 33 takbir, completing the hundred.
A light remembrance with a great reward.
evidence.Counting on fingers or with a counter: Counting on fingers or with a counter
evidence.Counting on the fingers is better, per t: Counting on the fingers is better, per the hadith «count on your fingertips, for they will be questioned and made to speak» (Abu Dawud 1501, al-Tirmidhi 3583); using beads or a counter is permissible according to most scholars.
evidence.Religious obligations such as prayer and: Religious obligations such as prayer and fasting begin at puberty.
evidence.If the signs of puberty do not appear, t: If the signs of puberty do not appear, the majority set it at fifteen Hijri years, per Ibn Umar's hadith in Bukhari (2664), and Abu Hanifa at eighteen. That is why the app also shows your age in Hijri years.
evidence.Your daily portion is according to your: Your daily portion is according to your ability; consistency is most beloved to Allah, even if little.
evidence.The app's khatma plans follow it: in a m: The app's khatma plans follow it: in a month, and in a week for whoever is able.
evidence.Every letter is a good deed, multiplied: Every letter is a good deed, multiplied tenfold.

mor01.t: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan, the accursed. Allah – there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is [presently] before them and what will be after them, and they encompass not a thing of His knowledge except for what He wills. His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation tires Him not. And He is the Most High, the Most Great.
mor01.narr: Ubayy ibn Ka'b (may Allah be pleased with him)
mor01.fadl: The jinn told Ubayy ibn Ka'b: “Whoever says it in the evening is protected from us until morning, and whoever says it in the morning is protected from us until evening.” When he told the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “The wicked one has spoken the truth.”

mor02.narr: Abdullah ibn Khubayb (may Allah be pleased with him)
mor02.fadl: “Say: Qul huwa Allahu ahad and the two Mu'awwidhat (al-Falaq and an-Nas) in the evening and in the morning, three times; they will suffice you against everything.”

mor03.t: We have reached the morning, and at this very time all sovereignty belongs to Allah, and all praise is for Allah. None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, alone, without partner; to Him belongs all sovereignty and praise, and He is over all things omnipotent. My Lord, I ask You for the good of what is in this day and the good of what follows it, and I take refuge in You from the evil of what is in this day and the evil of what follows it. My Lord, I take refuge in You from laziness and the misery of old age. My Lord, I take refuge in You from punishment in the Fire and punishment in the grave.
mor03.narr: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him)

mor04.t: O Allah, by You we have reached the morning and by You we have reached the evening; by You we live and by You we die, and to You is the resurrection.
mor04.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)

mor05.t: O Allah, You are my Lord; none has the right to be worshipped except You. You created me and I am Your servant, and I abide by Your covenant and promise as best I can. I take refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge Your favour upon me, and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me, for none forgives sins except You.
mor05.narr: Shaddad ibn Aws (may Allah be pleased with him)
mor05.fadl: “The master of seeking forgiveness is … Whoever says it during the day with firm faith in it and dies that day before evening will be among the people of Paradise.”
mor05.note: The master of all supplications for forgiveness (Sayyid al-Istighfar)

mor06.t: O Allah, I have reached the morning, and I call on You, the bearers of Your Throne, Your angels and all of Your creation to witness that You are Allah; none has the right to be worshipped except You, alone, without partner, and that Muhammad is Your servant and Messenger.
mor06.narr: Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him)
mor06.fadl: “Whoever says in the morning or the evening: ‘O Allah, I have reached the morning, calling You to witness …’, Allah frees a quarter of him from the Fire; whoever says it twice, Allah frees half of him; whoever says it three times, Allah frees three quarters of him; and if he says it four times, Allah frees him from the Fire.”
mor06.note: Its chain was graded hasan by Shaykh Ibn Baz (Tuhfat al-Akhyar); Shaykh al-Albani graded it weak.

mor07.t: O Allah, whatever blessing I or any of Your creation have this morning is from You alone, without partner; so to You belongs all praise and to You all thanks.
mor07.narr: Abdullah ibn Ghannam al-Bayadi (may Allah be pleased with him)
mor07.fadl: “Whoever says it in the morning … has fulfilled the thanks due for his day.”
mor07.note: Its chain was graded hasan by Shaykh Ibn Baz (Tuhfat al-Akhyar); Shaykh al-Albani graded it weak.

mor08.t: O Allah, grant my body well-being. O Allah, grant my hearing well-being. O Allah, grant my sight well-being. None has the right to be worshipped except You. O Allah, I take refuge in You from disbelief and poverty, and I take refuge in You from the punishment of the grave. None has the right to be worshipped except You.
mor08.narr: Abu Bakrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
mor08.fadl: When his son asked him why he repeated it three times morning and evening, Abu Bakrah said: “I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ supplicate with these words, and I love to follow his Sunnah.”

mor09.t: Allah is sufficient for me; none has the right to be worshipped except Him. Upon Him I rely, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne.
mor09.narr: Abu al-Darda' (may Allah be pleased with him)
mor09.fadl: “Whoever says, in the morning and in the evening, ‘Allah is sufficient for me … Lord of the Mighty Throne’ seven times, Allah will suffice him in whatever concerns him.”
mor09.note: Abu Dawud reports it as the saying of Abu al-Darda', Ibn al-Sunni as the Prophet's ﷺ words; Shu'ayb and Abd al-Qadir al-Arna'ut graded its chain sahih, while Shaykh al-Albani graded it weak.

mor10.t: O Allah, I ask You for pardon and well-being in this world and the Hereafter. O Allah, I ask You for pardon and well-being in my religion, my worldly affairs, my family and my wealth. O Allah, conceal my faults and calm my fears. O Allah, guard me from in front of me and behind me, from my right and my left, and from above me, and I seek refuge in Your greatness from being taken unawares from beneath me.
mor10.narr: Abdullah ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both)
mor10.fadl: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never left these supplications in the evening and in the morning.”

mor11.t: O Allah, Knower of the unseen and the seen, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Lord and Sovereign of all things, I bear witness that none has the right to be worshipped except You. I take refuge in You from the evil of my soul and from the evil of Satan and his snares (also narrated: his shirk), and from committing evil against myself or bringing it upon a Muslim.
mor11.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him): Abu Bakr al-Siddiq asked the Prophet ﷺ
mor11.fadl: “Say it in the morning, in the evening, and when you lie down to sleep.”

mor12.t: In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing on earth or in the heaven can cause harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
mor12.narr: Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him)
mor12.fadl: “There is no servant who says in the morning of every day and the evening of every night: ‘In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing … can cause harm …’ three times, and then anything harms him.”

mor13.t: I am pleased with Allah as my Lord, with Islam as my religion, and with Muhammad ﷺ as my Prophet.
mor13.narr: A servant of the Prophet ﷺ, reported by Abu Sallam
mor13.fadl: “There is no Muslim – or person, or servant – who says in the evening and in the morning: ‘I am pleased with Allah as my Lord, with Islam as my religion and with Muhammad as my Prophet’, except that it becomes a right upon Allah to please him on the Day of Resurrection.”
mor13.note: Three times, as in the narration of Ahmad and al-Nasa'i ('Amal al-Yawm wal-Laylah).

mor14.t: O Ever-Living, O Sustainer of all, by Your mercy I seek help: set right all my affairs for me, and do not leave me to myself even for the blink of an eye.
mor14.narr: Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him)
mor14.fadl: The Prophet ﷺ said to Fatimah (may Allah be pleased with her): “What prevents you from listening to what I advise you? That you say in the morning and in the evening: …”

mor15.t: We have reached the morning, and at this very time all sovereignty belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds. O Allah, I ask You for the good of this day: its opening, its victory, its light, its blessing and its guidance; and I take refuge in You from the evil of what is in it and the evil of what follows it.
mor15.narr: Abu Malik al-Ash'ari (may Allah be pleased with him)
mor15.fadl: “When one of you reaches the morning, let him say: ‘We have reached the morning and all sovereignty belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds …’ Then when he reaches the evening, let him say the same.”
mor15.note: Shu'ayb and Abd al-Qadir al-Arna'ut graded its chain hasan (in their edition of Zad al-Ma'ad); Shaykh al-Albani graded it weak.

mor16.t: We have reached the morning upon the fitrah of Islam, upon the word of sincere devotion (La ilaha illallah), upon the religion of our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and upon the way of our father Ibrahim, who was upright, a Muslim, and was not of those who associate partners with Allah.
mor16.narr: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza (may Allah be pleased with him)
mor16.note: The Prophet ﷺ used to say it upon reaching the morning.

mor17.t: How perfect Allah is, and I praise Him.
mor17.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
mor17.fadl: “Whoever says, in the morning and in the evening, ‘Subhan Allahi wa bihamdihi’ one hundred times, no one will come on the Day of Resurrection with anything better than what he brings, except someone who said the same or more.”

mor18.t: None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, alone, without partner. To Him belongs all sovereignty and all praise, and He is over all things omnipotent.
mor18.narr: Abu Ayyub al-Ansari (may Allah be pleased with him)
mor18.fadl: “Whoever says ‘None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, alone, without partner; to Him belongs all sovereignty and praise, and He is over all things omnipotent’ ten times is like one who has freed four souls from the descendants of Isma'il.”
mor18.note: Ten times, or once when feeling lazy. In the hadith of Abu 'Ayyash al-Zuraqi (Abu Dawud, Ibn Majah): whoever says it once in the morning is protected from Satan until evening, and if he says it in the evening he has the same until morning.

mor19.t: None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, alone, without partner. To Him belongs all sovereignty and all praise, and He is over all things omnipotent.
mor19.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
mor19.fadl: “Whoever says ‘None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, alone, without partner; to Him belongs all sovereignty and praise, and He is over all things omnipotent’ one hundred times in a day, it will be for him equal to freeing ten slaves; one hundred good deeds will be recorded for him and one hundred bad deeds erased; it will be a protection for him from Satan that day until evening; and no one will bring anything better than what he brings, except someone who did more.”
mor19.note: One hundred times, in the morning.

mor20.t: How perfect Allah is, and I praise Him, by the number of His creation, by His pleasure, by the weight of His Throne, and by the ink of His words.
mor20.narr: Juwayriyah bint al-Harith, Mother of the Believers (may Allah be pleased with her)
mor20.fadl: “After leaving you I said four phrases, three times, which, if weighed against all you have said since this morning, would outweigh it.”

mor21.t: O Allah, I ask You for beneficial knowledge, good provision, and deeds that are accepted.
mor21.narr: Umm Salamah, Mother of the Believers (may Allah be pleased with her)
mor21.note: In the morning; the Prophet ﷺ used to say it after the Fajr prayer, upon giving the salam.

mor22.t: I seek Allah's forgiveness and I turn to Him in repentance.
mor22.narr: Al-Agharr al-Muzani and Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with them)
mor22.fadl: “O people, repent to Allah, for I repent to Him one hundred times a day.”
mor22.note: One hundred times in the day. In al-Bukhari: “By Allah, I seek Allah's forgiveness and repent to Him more than seventy times a day.”

mor23.t: O Allah, send prayers and peace upon our Prophet Muhammad.
mor23.narr: Abu al-Darda' (may Allah be pleased with him)
mor23.fadl: “Whoever sends prayers upon me ten times in the morning and ten times in the evening, my intercession will reach him on the Day of Resurrection.”
mor23.note: Reported by al-Tabarani with two chains, one of which al-Mundhiri called good; al-Albani graded it hasan in Sahih al-Targhib (as cited by Hisn al-Muslim) but later graded it weak due to a break in the chain. The virtue of sending prayers upon the Prophet ﷺ in general is authentically established.

eve19.narr: Al-Agharr al-Muzani and Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with them)
eve19.fadl: “O people, repent to Allah, for I repent to Him one hundred times a day.”
eve19.note: One hundred times in the day. In al-Bukhari: “By Allah, I seek Allah's forgiveness and repent to Him more than seventy times a day.”

eve20.t: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created.
eve20.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
eve20.fadl: He ﷺ said to a man who had been stung by a scorpion: “Had you said in the evening, ‘I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created’, it would not have harmed you.”
eve20.note: Three times in the evening (the threefold repetition is in al-Tirmidhi's narration).

eve21.t: O Allah, send prayers and peace upon our Prophet Muhammad.
eve21.narr: Abu al-Darda' (may Allah be pleased with him)
eve21.fadl: “Whoever sends prayers upon me ten times in the morning and ten times in the evening, my intercession will reach him on the Day of Resurrection.”
eve21.note: Reported by al-Tabarani with two chains, one of which al-Mundhiri called good; al-Albani graded it hasan in Sahih al-Targhib (as cited by Hisn al-Muslim) but later graded it weak due to a break in the chain. The virtue of sending prayers upon the Prophet ﷺ in general is authentically established.

slp01.narr: Aishah, Mother of the Believers (may Allah be pleased with her)
slp01.note: He ﷺ would put his palms together, blow lightly into them and recite these surahs over them, then wipe as much of his body as he could, beginning with his head, face and the front of his body; he did this three times.

slp02.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
slp02.fadl: Satan told Abu Hurayrah: “When you go to your bed, recite Ayat al-Kursi … a guardian from Allah will remain over you and no devil will come near you until morning.” The Prophet ﷺ said: “He has told you the truth, though he is a great liar.”

slp03.narr: Abu Mas'ud al-Ansari al-Badri (may Allah be pleased with him)
slp03.fadl: “Whoever recites the last two verses of Surat al-Baqarah at night, they will suffice him.”

slp04.t: In Your name, my Lord, I lay down my side, and by You I raise it. If You take my soul, then have mercy on it; and if You send it back, then protect it with that with which You protect Your righteous servants.
slp04.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
slp04.fadl: “When one of you goes to his bed, let him dust off his bed with the inner edge of his lower garment, for he does not know what has come onto it after him; then let him say: …”

slp05.t: O Allah, You created my soul and You take it in death; to You belong its death and its life. If You keep it alive, then protect it, and if You cause it to die, then forgive it. O Allah, I ask You for well-being.
slp05.narr: Abdullah ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both)
slp05.note: Ibn Umar taught it to a man to say when lying down, and said he heard it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

slp06.t: O Allah, protect me from Your punishment on the Day You resurrect Your servants.
slp06.narr: Hafsah, Mother of the Believers (may Allah be pleased with her)
slp06.note: When he ﷺ wanted to sleep, he would place his right hand under his cheek and say it three times.

slp07.t: In Your name, O Allah, I die and I live.
slp07.narr: Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman and al-Bara' ibn Azib (may Allah be pleased with them)

slp08.narr: Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him)
slp08.fadl: “Shall I not teach you something better than what you asked me for? When you lie down to sleep, say Allahu akbar thirty-four times, Subhan Allah thirty-three times and Alhamdulillah thirty-three times; that is better for you than a servant.”

slp09.narr: Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him)

slp10.narr: Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him)

slp11.t: O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the earth, and Lord of the Mighty Throne, our Lord and Lord of all things, Splitter of the seed and the date-stone, Revealer of the Torah, the Gospel and the Criterion (the Qur'an): I take refuge in You from the evil of everything whose forelock You hold. O Allah, You are the First, so there is nothing before You; You are the Last, so there is nothing after You; You are the Most High (al-Zahir), so there is nothing above You; and You are the Most Near (al-Batin), so there is nothing beyond You. Settle our debt for us and free us from poverty.
slp11.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
slp11.note: He ﷺ instructed that when one lies down to sleep he should lie on his right side and then say this.

slp12.t: All praise is for Allah, who fed us and gave us drink, who sufficed us and sheltered us; for how many are there who have none to suffice them and none to shelter them.
slp12.narr: Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him)
slp12.note: He ﷺ used to say it when he went to his bed.

slp13.t: O Allah, Knower of the unseen and the seen, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Lord and Sovereign of all things, I bear witness that none has the right to be worshipped except You. I take refuge in You from the evil of my soul and from the evil of Satan and his shirk (his call to associate partners with Allah), and from committing evil against myself or bringing it upon a Muslim.
slp13.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him): Abu Bakr al-Siddiq asked the Prophet ﷺ
slp13.fadl: “Say it in the morning, in the evening, and when you lie down to sleep.”

slp14.t: Recite Surat as-Sajdah (Alif Lam Mim. Tanzil…, chapter 32) and Surat al-Mulk (Tabarak alladhi biyadihi al-mulk, chapter 67).
slp14.narr: Jabir ibn Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with them both)
slp14.fadl: “The Prophet ﷺ would not sleep until he had recited Alif Lam Mim Tanzil (as-Sajdah) and Tabarak alladhi biyadihi al-mulk (al-Mulk).”

slp15.t: O Allah, I submit my soul to You, I entrust my affair to You, I turn my face to You, and I lean my back on You, in hope of You and in fear of You. There is no refuge and no escape from You except to You. I believe in Your Book which You have revealed and in Your Prophet whom You have sent.
slp15.narr: Al-Bara' ibn Azib (may Allah be pleased with them both)
slp15.fadl: “When you go to your bed, perform wudu as you do for prayer, then lie on your right side and say: … If you die that night, you will die upon the fitrah; and make these the last words you say.”

slp16.t: None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, the One, the Subduer, Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, the Almighty, the Oft-Forgiving.
slp16.narr: Aishah, Mother of the Believers (may Allah be pleased with her)
slp16.note: The Prophet ﷺ used to say it when he turned over in his sleep at night.

slp17.t: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from His anger and His punishment, from the evil of His servants, and from the whisperings of the devils and from their coming to me.
slp17.narr: Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As (may Allah be pleased with them both)
slp17.fadl: “When one of you is frightened in his sleep, let him say: … and it will not harm him.”

slp18.t: Spit lightly (blowing with little spittle) to your left three times; seek refuge in Allah from Satan and from the evil of what you saw, three times; do not tell anyone about it; and turn over from the side you were lying on.
slp18.narr: Abu Qatadah and Jabir ibn Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with them)
slp18.fadl: “If he sees something he dislikes, let him spit lightly to his left three times, seek refuge in Allah from the evil of Satan and the evil of the dream, and not tell anyone about it; then it will not harm him.”
slp18.note: These are actions to be done by one who sees something he dislikes in his sleep.

slp19.t: Get up and pray, if one wishes.
slp19.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
slp19.fadl: “If one of you sees something he dislikes, let him get up and pray, and not tell people about it.”

wak01.t: All praise is for Allah, who gave us life after having caused us to die, and to Him is the resurrection.
wak01.narr: Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman and al-Bara' ibn Azib (may Allah be pleased with them)

wak02.t: None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, alone, without partner; to Him belongs all sovereignty and praise, and He is over all things omnipotent. How perfect Allah is, all praise is for Allah, none has the right to be worshipped except Allah, Allah is the Greatest, and there is no might nor power except with Allah, the Most High, the Most Great. My Lord, forgive me.
wak02.narr: Ubadah ibn al-Samit (may Allah be pleased with him)
wak02.fadl: “Whoever wakes up at night and says: … and then says, ‘O Allah, forgive me’, or makes a supplication, he will be answered; and if he performs wudu and prays, his prayer will be accepted.”
wak02.note: For one who wakes up during the night; the wording is that of Ibn Majah.

wak03.t: All praise is for Allah, who restored my body to health, returned my soul to me, and permitted me to remember Him.
wak03.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
wak03.fadl: “When he wakes up, let him say: ‘All praise is for Allah, who restored my body to health, returned my soul to me, and permitted me to remember Him.’”

wak04.narr: Abdullah ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both)
wak04.note: When the Prophet ﷺ got up at night, he would look up at the sky and recite these verses from the end of Surat Al Imran.

aft01.narr: Thawban, the freed servant of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (may Allah be pleased with him)
aft01.fadl: “When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished his prayer, he would seek forgiveness three times and say: O Allah, You are as-Salam and from You is all peace; blessed are You, O Possessor of majesty and honour.”

aft02.t: O Allah, You are as-Salam (the One free from every imperfection), and from You is all peace. Blessed are You, O Possessor of majesty and honour.
aft02.narr: Thawban, the freed servant of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (may Allah be pleased with him)

aft03.t: None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, alone, without partner; to Him belongs all sovereignty and praise, and He is over all things omnipotent. O Allah, none can withhold what You give, and none can give what You withhold, and the wealth and status of the wealthy cannot benefit them against You.
aft03.narr: Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah (may Allah be pleased with him)
aft03.fadl: “The Prophet ﷺ used to say after every obligatory prayer: …”
aft03.note: Hisn al-Muslim notes the first part (La ilaha illallah … qadir) is said three times.

aft04.t: None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, alone, without partner; to Him belongs all sovereignty and praise, and He is over all things omnipotent. There is no might nor power except with Allah. None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, and we worship none but Him. His is all blessing, His is all bounty, and His is all excellent praise. None has the right to be worshipped except Allah; we make our religion sincerely His, even though the disbelievers dislike it.
aft04.narr: Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr (may Allah be pleased with them both)
aft04.fadl: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to proclaim Allah's oneness with these words after every prayer.”

aft05.t: How perfect Allah is; all praise is for Allah; Allah is the Greatest.
aft05.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
aft05.fadl: “Whoever glorifies Allah after every prayer thirty-three times, praises Allah thirty-three times and declares His greatness thirty-three times – that is ninety-nine – and completes the hundred by saying: ‘None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, alone, without partner; to Him belongs all sovereignty and praise, and He is over all things omnipotent’, his sins will be forgiven even if they are like the foam of the sea.”
aft05.note: Thirty-three times (the three said together, or each one thirty-three times), then complete the hundred with the following.

aft06.t: None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, alone, without partner. To Him belongs all sovereignty and all praise, and He is over all things omnipotent.
aft06.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
aft06.note: Completes the hundred after the tasbih, tahmid and takbir.

aft07.narr: Uqbah ibn Amir (may Allah be pleased with him)
aft07.fadl: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded me to recite the Mu'awwidhat after every prayer.”
aft07.note: Once after every prayer, and three times after the Fajr and Maghrib prayers.

aft08.narr: Abu Umamah al-Bahili (may Allah be pleased with him)
aft08.fadl: “Whoever recites Ayat al-Kursi after every obligatory prayer, nothing prevents him from entering Paradise except death.”
aft08.note: Recited after every prayer (al-Nasa'i, 'Amal al-Yawm wal-Laylah).

aft09.t: None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, alone, without partner; to Him belongs all sovereignty and praise; He gives life and causes death, and He is over all things omnipotent.
aft09.narr: Abu Dharr al-Ghifari (may Allah be pleased with him)
aft09.fadl: “Whoever says after the Fajr prayer, while still sitting as he was and before speaking: … ten times, ten good deeds are recorded for him, ten bad deeds are erased, he is raised ten degrees, he is protected that whole day from every harm and guarded from Satan.”
aft09.note: Ten times after the Maghrib and Fajr prayers.

aft10.t: O Allah, I ask You for beneficial knowledge, good provision, and deeds that are accepted.
aft10.narr: Umm Salamah, Mother of the Believers (may Allah be pleased with her)
aft10.fadl: “The Prophet ﷺ used to say, after praying Fajr, upon giving the salam: …”
aft10.note: After the salam of the Fajr prayer.

aft11.t: How perfect is the King, the Most Holy.
aft11.narr: Ubayy ibn Ka'b (may Allah be pleased with him)
aft11.fadl: “When he finished (the Witr), he would say: ‘How perfect is the King, the Most Holy’ three times, lengthening the last of them.”
aft11.note: Three times, raising and drawing out the voice on the third and adding: “Rabbil-mala'ikati war-ruh” (Lord of the angels and the Spirit) – an addition reported by al-Daraqutni.

sal01.t: O Allah, put a distance between me and my sins as You have put a distance between the East and the West. O Allah, purify me of my sins as a white garment is purified of dirt. O Allah, wash away my sins with snow, water and hail.
sal01.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
sal01.note: Said after the opening takbir, before the recitation

sal02.t: How perfect You are, O Allah, and with Your praise. Blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is none worthy of worship besides You.
sal02.narr: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri and Aishah (may Allah be pleased with them)
sal02.note: Said after the opening takbir, before the recitation

sal03.t: I have turned my face towards the One who created the heavens and the earth, as a pure monotheist, and I am not of those who associate partners with Allah. Indeed my prayer, my sacrifice, my life and my death are for Allah, Lord of the worlds; He has no partner. With this I have been commanded, and I am of the Muslims. O Allah, You are the King; none has the right to be worshipped except You. You are my Lord and I am Your servant. I have wronged myself and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me all my sins, for none forgives sins except You. Guide me to the best of character, for none guides to the best of it except You, and turn away from me its evil, for none turns away its evil from me except You. Here I am at Your service, ready to obey You. All good is in Your hands, and evil is not attributed to You. I exist by You and I return to You. Blessed and Exalted are You. I seek Your forgiveness and I turn to You in repentance.
sal03.narr: Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him)
sal03.note: The Prophet ﷺ would say it when he stood for prayer

sal04.t: O Allah, Lord of Jibril, Mika'il and Israfil, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen, You judge between Your servants concerning that over which they used to differ. Guide me, by Your permission, to the truth in that over which they differed. Indeed You guide whom You will to a straight path.
sal04.narr: Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her)
sal04.note: The Prophet ﷺ would open his prayer with it when he rose at night

sal05.t: Allah is the Most Great, greatly (three times); much praise is for Allah (three times); and glory be to Allah morning and evening (three times). I seek refuge with Allah from the devil: from his arrogance, his poetry and his madness.
sal05.narr: Jubayr ibn Mut'im (may Allah be pleased with him); its core is in Muslim from Ibn Umar
sal05.fadl: “I marvelled at it: the gates of heaven were opened for it.” (Muslim, about saying: Allah is the Most Great, greatly; much praise is for Allah; glory be to Allah morning and evening)
sal05.note: The threefold repetition and the seeking of refuge are from Jubayr ibn Mut'im's hadith in Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah, whose chain has been discussed; the formula said once is established in Sahih Muslim from Ibn Umar

sal06.t: O Allah, to You belongs all praise; You are the Light of the heavens and the earth and all that is in them. To You belongs all praise; You are the Sustainer of the heavens and the earth and all that is in them. To You belongs all praise; You are the Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is in them. To You belongs all praise; Yours is the dominion of the heavens and the earth and all that is in them. To You belongs all praise; You are the King of the heavens and the earth. To You belongs all praise. You are the Truth, Your promise is true, Your word is true, the meeting with You is true, Paradise is true, the Fire is true, the Prophets are true, Muhammad ﷺ is true, and the Hour is true. O Allah, to You I have submitted, in You I have put my trust, in You I have believed, to You I have turned in repentance, by You I argue, and to You I turn for judgement. So forgive me what I have done before and what I will do after, what I have concealed and what I have done openly, and what You know better than I. You are the One who brings forward and the One who puts back; none has the right to be worshipped except You. You are my God; none has the right to be worshipped except You. There is no might nor power except with Allah.
sal06.narr: Abdullah ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him)
sal06.note: The Prophet ﷺ would say it when he rose for the night prayer (tahajjud); the wordings of the various narrations are combined here

sal07.t: How perfect is my Lord, the Most Great.
sal07.narr: Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman (may Allah be pleased with him)

sal08.t: How perfect You are, O Allah, our Lord, and with Your praise. O Allah, forgive me.
sal08.narr: Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her)
sal08.note: The Prophet ﷺ would often say it in his ruku' and sujud

sal09.t: Perfect and Holy is He, Lord of the angels and of the Spirit (Jibril).
sal09.narr: Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her)

sal10.t: O Allah, to You I have bowed, in You I have believed, and to You I have submitted. My hearing, my sight, my brain, my bones, my sinews, and all that my feet carry are humbled before You.
sal10.narr: Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him)
sal10.note: The phrase “and all that my feet carry” is not in Sahih Muslim; it is in a narration in the Musnad of Ahmad

sal11.t: How perfect is the Possessor of might, dominion, grandeur and majesty.
sal11.narr: Awf ibn Malik al-Ashja'i (may Allah be pleased with him)

sal12.t: Allah hears the one who praises Him.
sal12.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)

sal13.t: Our Lord, and to You belongs all praise: abundant, good and blessed praise.
sal13.narr: Rifa'ah ibn Rafi' al-Zuraqi (may Allah be pleased with him)
sal13.fadl: “I saw over thirty angels racing to be the first to write it down.”
sal13.note: Said after standing up straight from ruku'

sal14.t: Filling the heavens, filling the earth and all that is between them, and filling whatever else You will. O You who are worthy of praise and glory, the truest thing a servant has said, and we are all Your servants: O Allah, none can withhold what You give, none can give what You withhold, and the wealth of the wealthy cannot avail him against You.
sal14.narr: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him)
sal14.note: Said after “Our Lord, and to You belongs all praise”

sal15.t: How perfect is my Lord, the Most High.
sal15.narr: Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman (may Allah be pleased with him)

sal16.t: How perfect You are, O Allah, our Lord, and with Your praise. O Allah, forgive me.
sal16.narr: Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her)
sal16.note: The Prophet ﷺ would often say it in his ruku' and sujud

sal17.t: Perfect and Holy is He, Lord of the angels and of the Spirit (Jibril).
sal17.narr: Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her)

sal18.t: O Allah, to You I have prostrated, in You I have believed, and to You I have submitted. My face has prostrated to the One who created it, fashioned it, and brought forth its hearing and sight. Blessed is Allah, the best of creators.
sal18.narr: Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him)

sal19.t: How perfect is the Possessor of might, dominion, grandeur and majesty.
sal19.narr: Awf ibn Malik al-Ashja'i (may Allah be pleased with him)

sal20.t: O Allah, forgive me all my sins: the small and the great, the first and the last, the open and the secret.
sal20.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
sal20.fadl: “The closest a servant is to his Lord is while he is prostrating, so make abundant supplication.” (Muslim 482)

sal21.t: O Allah, I seek refuge in Your pleasure from Your anger, and in Your pardon from Your punishment, and I seek refuge in You from You. I cannot count Your praise; You are as You have praised Yourself.
sal21.narr: Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her)

sal22.t: My Lord, forgive me. My Lord, forgive me.
sal22.narr: Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman (may Allah be pleased with him)

sal23.t: O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, guide me, mend my affairs, grant me well-being, provide for me, and raise my rank.
sal23.narr: Abdullah ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him)
sal23.note: The wordings of Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah are combined here

sal24.t: My face has prostrated to the One who created it and brought forth its hearing and sight by His might and power. So blessed is Allah, the best of creators.
sal24.narr: Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her)
sal24.note: The Prophet ﷺ would say it in the prostration of recitation at night. The phrase “So blessed is Allah, the best of creators” is an addition in al-Hakim, who graded it sahih, and al-Dhahabi agreed

sal25.t: O Allah, record for me a reward with You for it, remove from me a sin by it, store it for me with You as a treasure, and accept it from me as You accepted it from Your servant Dawud.
sal25.narr: Abdullah ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him)

sal26.t: All greetings are for Allah, and all prayers and all good things. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah. I bear witness that none has the right to be worshipped except Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.
sal26.narr: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him)

sal27.t: O Allah, send prayers upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent prayers upon Ibrahim and upon the family of Ibrahim; You are indeed Praiseworthy, Glorious. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon Ibrahim and upon the family of Ibrahim; You are indeed Praiseworthy, Glorious.
sal27.narr: Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah (may Allah be pleased with him)

sal28.t: O Allah, send prayers upon Muhammad and upon his wives and his offspring, as You sent prayers upon the family of Ibrahim; and send blessings upon Muhammad and upon his wives and his offspring, as You sent blessings upon the family of Ibrahim. You are indeed Praiseworthy, Glorious.
sal28.narr: Abu Humayd al-Sa'idi (may Allah be pleased with him)

sal29.t: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave, from the punishment of Hell, from the trials of life and death, and from the evil of the trial of the False Messiah (al-Dajjal).
sal29.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
sal29.fadl: “When one of you finishes the final tashahhud, let him seek refuge with Allah from four things.” (Muslim)

sal30.t: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave, I seek refuge in You from the trial of the False Messiah, and I seek refuge in You from the trials of life and death. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from sin and from debt.
sal30.narr: Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her)
sal30.note: The Prophet ﷺ would supplicate with it in the prayer

sal31.t: O Allah, I have wronged myself greatly, and none forgives sins except You, so grant me forgiveness from Yourself and have mercy on me. You are indeed the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful.
sal31.narr: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him)
sal31.fadl: Abu Bakr said to the Prophet ﷺ: “Teach me a supplication to say in my prayer.” He said: “Say: …”

sal32.t: O Allah, forgive me what I have done before and what I will do after, what I have concealed and what I have done openly, what I have done in excess, and what You know better than I. You are the One who brings forward and the One who puts back; none has the right to be worshipped except You.
sal32.narr: Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him)
sal32.note: It was among the last things the Prophet ﷺ would say between the tashahhud and the taslim

sal33.t: O Allah, help me to remember You, to thank You, and to worship You well.
sal33.narr: Mu'adh ibn Jabal (may Allah be pleased with him)
sal33.fadl: “O Mu'adh, by Allah I love you… Do not fail to say at the end of every prayer: …”

sal34.t: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from miserliness, I seek refuge in You from cowardice, I seek refuge in You from being returned to the most decrepit old age, and I seek refuge in You from the trials of this world and the punishment of the grave.
sal34.narr: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (may Allah be pleased with him)
sal34.note: The Prophet ﷺ would seek refuge with these at the end of the prayer

sal35.t: O Allah, I ask You for Paradise and I seek refuge in You from the Fire.
sal35.narr: A man from the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ; Ibn Majah narrates it from Abu Hurayrah
sal35.fadl: The man said: “I cannot murmur as you do nor as Mu'adh does.” The Prophet ﷺ said: “It is around this that we murmur.”

sal36.t: O Allah, by Your knowledge of the unseen and Your power over creation, keep me alive as long as You know life is good for me, and take me when You know death is good for me. O Allah, I ask You for fear of You in private and in public, for a word of truth in contentment and in anger, and for moderation in wealth and in poverty. I ask You for bliss that never ends and for a delight of the eye that never ceases. I ask You for contentment after Your decree, for a pleasant life after death, and for the delight of looking at Your Face and longing to meet You, without harmful adversity or misleading trial. O Allah, adorn us with the adornment of faith and make us guides who are rightly guided.
sal36.narr: Ammar ibn Yasir (may Allah be pleased with him)

sal37.t: O Allah, I ask You, O Allah, as You are the One, the Unique, the Self-Sufficient, who neither begets nor was begotten, and to whom no one is equal, to forgive me my sins. You are indeed the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful.
sal37.narr: Mihjan ibn al-Adra' (may Allah be pleased with him)
sal37.fadl: “He has been forgiven, he has been forgiven” (three times)
sal37.note: The Prophet ﷺ heard a man saying it in his tashahhud

sal38.t: O Allah, I ask You, as all praise is Yours; none has the right to be worshipped except You alone, without partner, the Bestower of favours. O Originator of the heavens and the earth, O Possessor of majesty and honour, O Ever-Living, O Sustainer of all, I ask You for Paradise and I seek refuge in You from the Fire.
sal38.narr: Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him)
sal38.fadl: “He has called upon Allah by His Greatest Name, by which, when He is called, He answers, and when He is asked, He gives.”

sal39.t: O Allah, I ask You, as I bear witness that You are Allah; none has the right to be worshipped except You, the One, the Self-Sufficient, who neither begets nor was begotten, and to whom no one is equal.
sal39.narr: Buraydah ibn al-Husayb (may Allah be pleased with him)
sal39.fadl: “You have asked Allah by the Name by which, when He is asked, He gives, and when He is called, He answers.”

adh01.t: There is no might nor power except with Allah.
adh01.narr: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri and Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with them)
adh01.fadl: “… from his heart, he will enter Paradise.” (Muslim, about the one who answers the mu'adhdhin)
adh01.note: Repeat what the mu'adhdhin says, except at “Hayya 'ala al-salah” and “Hayya 'ala al-falah”, where you say: There is no might nor power except with Allah

adh02.t: And I too bear witness that none has the right to be worshipped except Allah alone, without partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. I am pleased with Allah as Lord, with Muhammad as Messenger, and with Islam as religion.
adh02.narr: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (may Allah be pleased with him)
adh02.note: Said right after the mu'adhdhin's testimony of faith

adh03.t: O Allah, send prayers upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent prayers upon Ibrahim and upon the family of Ibrahim; You are indeed Praiseworthy, Glorious. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon Ibrahim and upon the family of Ibrahim; You are indeed Praiseworthy, Glorious.
adh03.narr: Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As (may Allah be pleased with him)
adh03.fadl: “When you hear the mu'adhdhin, say what he says, then send prayers upon me, for whoever sends one prayer upon me, Allah sends ten upon him.”
adh03.note: Send prayers upon the Prophet ﷺ after finishing answering the mu'adhdhin; the most complete form is the Ibrahimi prayer

adh04.t: O Allah, Lord of this perfect call and of the prayer about to be established, grant Muhammad al-wasilah (a station in Paradise) and al-fadilah (a rank above all creation), and raise him to the praised station that You have promised him.
adh04.narr: Jabir ibn Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him)
adh04.fadl: “Whoever says, upon hearing the call: … my intercession will be his on the Day of Resurrection.”
adh04.note: Al-Bayhaqi adds at the end: “Indeed You do not break Your promise”; Ibn Baz graded its chain hasan, while al-Albani considered it an irregular (shadh) addition

adh05.t: Supplication made between the adhan and the iqamah is not rejected.
adh05.narr: Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him)
adh05.note: This is not a specific formula but an encouragement to supplicate for yourself, for whatever you wish, between the adhan and the iqamah

msj01.t: O Allah, place light in my heart, light on my tongue, light in my hearing, and light in my sight; place light above me, light below me, light on my right, light on my left, light in front of me, and light behind me; place light in my soul; magnify light for me, increase light for me, grant me light and make me light. O Allah, give me light, and place light in my sinews, light in my flesh, light in my blood, light in my hair, and light in my skin.
msj01.narr: Abdullah ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him)
msj01.note: In Muslim's narration the Prophet ﷺ went out to the Fajr prayer saying it. Other narrations add, as cited in Hisn al-Muslim: “O Allah, place light for me in my grave… and light in my bones”, “and increase me in light” (three times), and “grant me light upon light”

msj02.t: I seek refuge with Allah the Almighty, with His Noble Face and His eternal authority, from the accursed devil.
msj02.narr: Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As (may Allah be pleased with him)
msj02.fadl: “When he says that, the devil says: He has been protected from me for the rest of the day.”
msj02.note: Enter the mosque with the right foot

msj03.t: In the name of Allah, and prayers and peace be upon the Messenger of Allah. O Allah, open for me the gates of Your mercy.
msj03.narr: Abu Humayd al-Sa'idi or Abu Usayd (may Allah be pleased with them)
msj03.note: “O Allah, open for me the gates of Your mercy” is in Sahih Muslim; the instruction to send peace upon the Prophet ﷺ before it is in Abu Dawud, and the basmalah is in Ibn al-Sunni

msj04.t: In the name of Allah, and prayers and peace be upon the Messenger of Allah. O Allah, I ask You of Your bounty. O Allah, protect me from the accursed devil.
msj04.narr: Abu Humayd al-Sa'idi or Abu Usayd, and Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with them)
msj04.note: Leave with the left foot. The phrase “O Allah, protect me from the accursed devil” is in Ibn Majah

qdu01.t: Our Lord, accept [this] from us. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing. Our Lord, and make us Muslims [in submission] to You and from our descendants a Muslim nation [in submission] to You. And show us our rites and accept our repentance. Indeed, You are the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.
qdu01.note: Supplication of Ibrahim and Isma'il (peace be upon them)

qdu02.t: Our Lord, give us in this world [that which is] good and in the Hereafter [that which is] good and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.
qdu02.note: Supplication of the believers; it was the supplication the Prophet ﷺ made most often

qdu03.t: Our Lord, pour upon us patience and plant firmly our feet and give us victory over the disbelieving people.
qdu03.note: Supplication of the believers in Talut's army when facing Jalut

qdu04.t: Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we have forgotten or erred. Our Lord, and lay not upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us. Our Lord, and burden us not with that which we have no ability to bear. And pardon us; and forgive us; and have mercy upon us. You are our protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people.
qdu04.note: Supplication of the believers at the end of Surat al-Baqarah

qdu05.t: Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate after You have guided us and grant us from Yourself mercy. Indeed, You are the Bestower.
qdu05.note: Supplication of those firm in knowledge

qdu06.t: Our Lord, indeed we have believed, so forgive us our sins and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.

qdu07.t: Our Lord, we have believed in what You revealed and have followed the messenger, so register us among the witnesses [to truth].
qdu07.note: Supplication of the disciples, the helpers of 'Isa (peace be upon him)

qdu08.t: Our Lord, forgive us our sins and the excess [committed] in our affairs and plant firmly our feet and give us victory over the disbelieving people.
qdu08.note: Supplication of the godly people who fought alongside the prophets

qdu09.t: Our Lord, You did not create this aimlessly; exalted are You [above such a thing]; then protect us from the punishment of the Fire. Our Lord, indeed whoever You admit to the Fire — You have disgraced him, and for the wrongdoers there are no helpers. Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith, [saying], ‘Believe in your Lord,’ and we have believed. Our Lord, so forgive us our sins and remove from us our misdeeds and cause us to die with the righteous. Our Lord, and grant us what You promised us through Your messengers and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, You do not fail in [Your] promise.
qdu09.note: Supplication of the people of understanding who reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth

qdu10.t: Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers.
qdu10.note: Supplication of Adam and Hawwa' (peace be upon them)

qdu11.t: Our Lord, pour upon us patience and let us die as Muslims [in submission to You].
qdu11.note: Supplication of Pharaoh's magicians after they believed

qdu12.t: Our Lord, make us not [objects of] trial for the wrongdoing people. And save us by Your mercy from the disbelieving people.
qdu12.note: Supplication of the people of Musa (peace be upon him)

qdu13.t: My Lord, make me an establisher of prayer, and [many] from my descendants. Our Lord, and accept my supplication. Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers the Day the account is established.
qdu13.note: Supplication of Ibrahim (peace be upon him)

qdu14.t: My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up [when I was] small.
qdu14.note: Supplication for parents which Allah commands children to make

qdu15.t: My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance and to exit a sound exit and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority.
qdu15.note: A supplication Allah commanded His Prophet ﷺ to make

qdu16.t: Our Lord, grant us from Yourself mercy and prepare for us from our affair right guidance.
qdu16.note: Supplication of the People of the Cave

qdu17.t: My Lord, expand for me my breast [with assurance] and ease for me my task and untie the knot from my tongue that they may understand my speech.
qdu17.note: Supplication of Musa (peace be upon him)

qdu18.t: My Lord, increase me in knowledge.
qdu18.note: A supplication Allah taught His Prophet ﷺ

qdu19.t: Indeed, adversity has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful.
qdu19.note: Supplication of Ayyub (peace be upon him)

qdu20.t: There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers.
qdu20.note: Supplication of Yunus (Dhu al-Nun, peace be upon him) in the belly of the whale

qdu21.t: My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the incitements of the devils, and I seek refuge in You, my Lord, lest they be present with me.
qdu21.note: Seeking refuge which Allah commanded His Prophet ﷺ to say

qdu22.t: Our Lord, we have believed, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the best of the merciful.
qdu22.note: Supplication of a party of Allah's believing servants

qdu23.t: My Lord, forgive and have mercy, and You are the best of the merciful.
qdu23.note: A supplication Allah commanded His Prophet ﷺ to make

qdu24.t: Our Lord, avert from us the punishment of Hell. Indeed, its punishment is ever adhering; indeed, it is evil as a settlement and residence.
qdu24.note: Supplication of the servants of the Most Merciful

qdu25.t: Our Lord, grant us from among our wives and offspring comfort to our eyes and make us a leader for the righteous.
qdu25.note: Supplication of the servants of the Most Merciful

qdu26.t: My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents and to do righteousness of which You approve. And admit me by Your mercy into [the ranks of] Your righteous servants.
qdu26.note: Supplication of Sulayman (peace be upon him)

qdu27.t: My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You would send down to me, in need.
qdu27.note: Supplication of Musa (peace be upon him) in Madyan

qdu28.t: Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who have repented and followed Your way and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire. Our Lord, and admit them to gardens of perpetual residence which You have promised them and whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses and their offspring. Indeed, it is You who is the Exalted in Might, the Wise. And protect them from the evil consequences [of their deeds]. And he whom You protect from evil consequences that Day — You will have given him mercy. And that is the great attainment.
qdu28.note: Supplication of the angels who bear the Throne, for the believers

qdu29.t: My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents and to work righteousness of which You will approve and make righteous for me my offspring. Indeed, I have repented to You, and indeed, I am of the Muslims.
qdu29.note: Supplication of the believer when he reaches maturity and forty years

qdu30.t: Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith and put not in our hearts [any] resentment toward those who have believed. Our Lord, indeed You are Kind and Merciful.
qdu30.note: Supplication of those who came after the Muhajirun and the Ansar

qdu31.t: Our Lord, upon You we have relied, and to You we have returned, and to You is the destination. Our Lord, make us not [objects of] torment for the disbelievers and forgive us, our Lord. Indeed, it is You who is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
qdu31.note: Supplication of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and those with him

qdu32.t: Our Lord, perfect for us our light and forgive us. Indeed, You are over all things competent.
qdu32.note: Supplication of the believers on the Day of Resurrection

qdu33.t: My Lord, forgive me and my parents and whoever enters my house a believer and the believing men and believing women. And do not increase the wrongdoers except in destruction.
qdu33.note: Supplication of Nuh (peace be upon him)

stg01.t: I seek Allah's forgiveness and I turn to Him in repentance.
stg01.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
stg01.fadl: “By Allah, I seek Allah's forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance more than seventy times a day.”
stg01.note: The Prophet ﷺ said it more than seventy times a day

stg02.narr: Al-Agharr al-Muzani (may Allah be pleased with him)
stg02.fadl: “My heart becomes clouded, and I seek Allah's forgiveness a hundred times a day.” In another narration: “O people, repent to Allah, for I repent to Him a hundred times a day.”
stg02.note: “Clouded”: Ibn al-Athir said it refers to moments of distraction from his constant remembrance, which he ﷺ counted against himself and so hastened to seek forgiveness

stg03.t: I seek the forgiveness of Allah the Mighty, besides whom none has the right to be worshipped except Him, the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting, and I turn to Him in repentance.
stg03.narr: Zayd, the freed slave of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (may Allah be pleased with him)
stg03.fadl: “Whoever says: I seek the forgiveness of Allah the Mighty, besides whom none has the right to be worshipped except Him, the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting, and I turn to Him in repentance — he will be forgiven even if he had fled from the battlefield.”
stg03.note: The word “the Mighty” is in al-Tirmidhi's narration, not in Abu Dawud's

stg04.t: The closest that the Lord comes to His servant is in the last part of the night, so if you are able to be among those who remember Allah at that hour, then do so.
stg04.narr: 'Amr ibn 'Abasah (may Allah be pleased with him)
stg04.note: A hadith on the virtue of remembrance and seeking forgiveness in the last part of the night — read it to act upon it

stg05.t: The closest a servant is to his Lord is while he is prostrating, so supplicate much [in it].
stg05.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
stg05.note: A hadith on the virtue of supplicating in prostration — read it to act upon it

stg06.t: There is no servant who commits a sin, then purifies himself well, then stands and prays two rak'ahs, then seeks Allah's forgiveness, except that Allah forgives him.
stg06.narr: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him)
stg06.note: What to do after a sin: perform ablution, pray two rak'ahs, then seek Allah's forgiveness. The Prophet ﷺ then recited: “And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins” (3:135)

tsb01.t: Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him.
tsb01.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
tsb01.fadl: “Whoever says ‘Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him’ a hundred times in a day, his sins will be wiped away even if they are like the foam of the sea.”

tsb02.t: None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, alone, without partner. To Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs all praise, and He is over all things competent.
tsb02.narr: Abu Ayyub al-Ansari (may Allah be pleased with him)
tsb02.fadl: “Whoever says: None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, alone, without partner; to Him belongs the dominion and all praise, and He is over all things competent — ten times, it is as if he freed four souls from the descendants of Isma'il.”

tsb03.t: Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him; glory be to Allah the Magnificent.
tsb03.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
tsb03.fadl: “Two words are light on the tongue, heavy on the Scale, and beloved to the Most Merciful: Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him; glory be to Allah the Magnificent.”

tsb04.t: Glory be to Allah, all praise is for Allah, none has the right to be worshipped except Allah, and Allah is the Greatest.
tsb04.narr: Abu Hurayrah and Samurah ibn Jundub (may Allah be pleased with them)
tsb04.fadl: “That I say: Glory be to Allah, all praise is for Allah, none has the right to be worshipped except Allah, and Allah is the Greatest — is more beloved to me than all that the sun rises upon.” And he ﷺ said: “The most beloved words to Allah are four: Glory be to Allah, all praise is for Allah, none has the right to be worshipped except Allah, and Allah is the Greatest. It does not matter which of them you begin with.”

tsb05.narr: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (may Allah be pleased with him)
tsb05.fadl: “Is any of you unable to earn a thousand good deeds each day?” One of those sitting with him asked: How can one of us earn a thousand good deeds? He said: “He glorifies Allah a hundred times, and a thousand good deeds are recorded for him, or a thousand sins are wiped away from him.”

tsb06.t: Glory be to Allah the Magnificent, and praise be to Him.
tsb06.narr: Jabir ibn 'Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with them both)
tsb06.fadl: “Whoever says ‘Glory be to Allah the Magnificent, and praise be to Him,’ a palm tree is planted for him in Paradise.”

tsb07.t: There is no might and no power except with Allah.
tsb07.narr: Abu Musa al-Ash'ari ('Abdullah ibn Qays) (may Allah be pleased with him)
tsb07.fadl: “O 'Abdullah ibn Qays, shall I not direct you to a treasure from the treasures of Paradise?” I said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said: “Say: There is no might and no power except with Allah.”

tsb08.t: None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, alone, without partner. Allah is the Greatest, greatly; much praise is for Allah; glory be to Allah, Lord of the worlds; there is no might and no power except with Allah, the Almighty, the Wise. O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, guide me and provide for me.
tsb08.narr: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (may Allah be pleased with him)
tsb08.fadl: A Bedouin came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: Teach me words to say … He said: These are for my Lord, so what is for me? He said: “Say: O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, guide me and provide for me.”

tsb09.t: O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, guide me, grant me well-being and provide for me.
tsb09.narr: Tariq ibn Ashyam al-Ashja'i (may Allah be pleased with him)
tsb09.fadl: When a man accepted Islam, the Prophet ﷺ would teach him the prayer, then instruct him to supplicate with these words. In another narration: “For these gather for you [the good of] your worldly life and your Hereafter.”

tsb10.t: None has the right to be worshipped except Allah.
tsb10.narr: Jabir ibn 'Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with them both)
tsb10.fadl: “The best supplication is: All praise is for Allah, and the best remembrance is: None has the right to be worshipped except Allah.”

tsb11.narr: Jabir ibn 'Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with them both)
tsb11.fadl: “The best supplication is: All praise is for Allah, and the best remembrance is: None has the right to be worshipped except Allah.”

tsb12.t: Glory be to Allah, all praise is for Allah, none has the right to be worshipped except Allah, Allah is the Greatest, and there is no might and no power except with Allah.
tsb12.narr: 'Uthman ibn 'Affan and Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with them)
tsb12.note: These are “the enduring good deeds” mentioned in: “But the enduring good deeds are better to your Lord for reward” (18:46). Ahmad (513) from 'Uthman; Abu Sa'id's narration was authenticated by Ibn Hibban and al-Hakim, as Ibn Hajar noted in Bulugh al-Maram

tsb13.t: I saw the Prophet ﷺ counting the tasbih [on his fingers] — and in an additional narration: with his right hand.
tsb13.narr: 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr (may Allah be pleased with them both)
tsb13.note: How the Prophet ﷺ glorified Allah: he counted his tasbih on the fingers of his right hand

tsb14.t: O Allah, send prayers upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent prayers upon Ibrahim and upon the family of Ibrahim; indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.
