O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon Ibrahim and upon the family of Ibrahim; indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.
tsb14.narr: Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
tsb14.fadl: They said: O Messenger of Allah, we have learned how to send greetings of peace upon you, so how do we send prayers upon you? He said: “Say: …”
tsb14.note: The Ibrahimi salawat, said in the tashahhud and at other times

tsb15.t: O Allah, send prayers upon Muhammad and upon his wives and his descendants, as You sent prayers upon the family of Ibrahim; and send blessings upon Muhammad and upon his wives and his descendants, as You sent blessings upon the family of Ibrahim; indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.
tsb15.narr: Abu Humayd al-Sa'idi (may Allah be pleased with him)

tsb16.t: Whoever sends one prayer upon me, Allah sends ten prayers upon him for it.
tsb16.narr: 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr (may Allah be pleased with them both)
tsb16.note: A hadith on the virtue of sending prayers upon the Prophet ﷺ — read it to act upon it

tsb17.t: Do not make my grave a place of festivity, and send prayers upon me, for your prayers reach me wherever you are.
tsb17.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
tsb17.note: A hadith on the virtue of sending prayers upon the Prophet ﷺ — read it to act upon it

tsb18.t: The miser is the one in whose presence I am mentioned and he does not send prayers upon me.
tsb18.narr: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him)
tsb18.note: A hadith on the virtue of sending prayers upon the Prophet ﷺ — read it to act upon it

tsb19.t: Allah has angels who roam the earth and convey to me the greetings of peace from my Ummah.
tsb19.narr: 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him)
tsb19.note: A hadith on the virtue of sending prayers upon the Prophet ﷺ — read it to act upon it

tsb20.t: There is no one who sends greetings of peace upon me except that Allah returns my soul to me so that I may return his greeting.
tsb20.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
tsb20.note: A hadith on the virtue of sending prayers upon the Prophet ﷺ — read it to act upon it

ram01.t: Allah is the Most Great. O Allah, bring it over us with security and faith, with safety and Islam, and with success in what You love and are pleased with, our Lord. Our Lord and your Lord is Allah.
ram01.narr: Talhah ibn Ubaydullah and Abdullah ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them)
ram01.note: On sighting the new crescent. This is al-Darimi's wording from Ibn Umar; al-Tirmidhi's wording from Talhah is: “O Allah, bring it over us with blessing and faith, with safety and Islam. My Lord and your Lord is Allah.”

ram02.t: The thirst has gone, the veins are moistened, and the reward is confirmed, if Allah wills.
ram02.narr: Abdullah ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with him)
ram02.note: The Prophet ﷺ would say it when he broke his fast. As for “O Allah, for You I fasted and with Your provision I break my fast”, Abu Dawud (2358) narrates it as a mursal report from Mu'adh ibn Zuhrah, and it is weak

ram03.t: O Allah, I ask You by Your mercy which encompasses all things to forgive me.
ram03.narr: Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As (may Allah be pleased with him)
ram03.fadl: “The fasting person, when breaking the fast, has a supplication that is not rejected.”
ram03.note: Abdullah ibn Amr used to say this when breaking his fast (his own practice). Ibn Hajar graded it hasan in Takhrij al-Adhkar, while al-Albani graded it weak (Irwa' al-Ghalil 921). The hadith “Three people's supplications are not rejected: the fasting person until he breaks his fast…” is narrated by al-Tirmidhi (3598), who graded it hasan, and Ibn Majah (1752); its chain contains Abu Mudillah, who is little known. Al-Albani graded sahih the wording: “Three supplications are not rejected: the supplication of a parent, of the fasting person and of the traveller” (al-Bayhaqi; al-Silsilah al-Sahihah)

ram04.t: May fasting people break their fast with you, may the righteous eat your food, and may the angels send prayers upon you.
ram04.narr: Anas ibn Malik and Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr (may Allah be pleased with them)
ram04.note: A supplication for the household with whom you broke your fast

ram05.t: When one of you is invited, let him accept. If he is fasting, let him supplicate (for them), and if he is not fasting, let him eat.
ram05.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
ram05.note: This is guidance rather than a formula to recite: “let him pray” means let him supplicate for the hosts for blessing and forgiveness

ram06.t: I am fasting, I am fasting.
ram06.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
ram06.fadl: “Fasting is a shield, so let him not speak obscenely nor act ignorantly. If someone fights him or insults him, let him say: I am fasting — twice.”
ram06.note: When someone insults or fights you while you are fasting

ram07.t: O Allah, You are Pardoning and You love to pardon, so pardon me.
ram07.narr: Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her)
ram07.fadl: She said: “O Messenger of Allah, if I know which night is Laylat al-Qadr, what should I say in it?” He said: “Say: …”
ram07.note: Say it often in the last ten nights of Ramadan. The word “Karim” after “'Afuww” is not in the reliable narrations, so it is not added

krb01.t: O Allah, I am Your servant, son of Your servant, son of Your maidservant. My forelock is in Your hand, Your judgement upon me is ever executed, and Your decree upon me is just. I ask You by every name that is Yours, with which You have named Yourself, or revealed in Your Book, or taught to any of Your creation, or kept to Yourself in the knowledge of the unseen with You, that You make the Quran the spring of my heart, the light of my chest, the removal of my sorrow and the departure of my worry.
krb01.narr: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him)
krb01.fadl: “No one is ever afflicted by worry or grief and says (this) except that Allah removes his worry and grief and replaces it with relief.”

krb02.t: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from worry and grief, from incapacity and laziness, from miserliness and cowardice, and from the burden of debt and being overpowered by men.
krb02.narr: Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him)
krb02.note: The Prophet ﷺ used to say it often. The author also lists it under supplications for settling a debt

krb03.t: None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, the Magnificent, the Forbearing. None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, Lord of the Magnificent Throne. None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, Lord of the heavens, Lord of the earth, and Lord of the Noble Throne.
krb03.narr: Abdullah ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both)
krb03.note: The Prophet ﷺ used to say it in times of distress

krb04.t: O Allah, it is Your mercy that I hope for, so do not leave me to myself even for the blink of an eye, and set right all my affairs. None has the right to be worshipped except You.
krb04.narr: Abu Bakrah Nufay‘ ibn al-Harith (may Allah be pleased with him)
krb04.fadl: “The supplications of the one in distress are: ‘O Allah, it is Your mercy that I hope for…’”

krb05.t: None has the right to be worshipped except You. How perfect You are; verily I have been among the wrongdoers.
krb05.narr: Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas (may Allah be pleased with him)
krb05.fadl: “The supplication of Dhun-Nun (Yunus) when he called out from the belly of the whale: ‘None has the right to be worshipped except You; how perfect You are, verily I have been among the wrongdoers.’ No Muslim ever supplicates with it for anything except that Allah answers him.”

krb06.t: Allah, Allah is my Lord; I do not associate anything with Him.
krb06.narr: Asma’ bint ‘Umays (may Allah be pleased with her)
krb06.fadl: “Shall I not teach you words to say at a time of distress: ‘Allah, Allah is my Lord; I do not associate anything with Him’?”

krb07.t: O Allah, we place You before them (to repel them), and we seek refuge in You from their evil.
krb07.narr: Abu Musa al-Ash‘ari (may Allah be pleased with him)
krb07.note: The Prophet ﷺ said it when he feared a people

krb08.t: O Allah, You are my support and You are my helper. By You I move, by You I attack, and by You I fight.
krb08.narr: Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him)
krb08.note: The Prophet ﷺ said it when going out to battle

krb09.t: Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.
krb09.narr: Abdullah ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both)
krb09.fadl: “‘Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs’ — Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said it when he was thrown into the fire, and Muhammad ﷺ said it when they said: ‘The people have gathered against you, so fear them.’”

krb10.t: O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the Magnificent Throne, be my protector against so-and-so son of so-and-so and his allies among Your creation, lest any of them should hasten to harm me or transgress against me. Mighty is the one under Your protection, glorious is Your praise, and none has the right to be worshipped except You.
krb10.narr: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him), as his own statement (mawquf)
krb10.note: Said by one who fears the oppression of a ruler; mention the person’s name in place of “so-and-so son of so-and-so”

krb11.t: Allah is the greatest. Allah is mightier than all His creation. Allah is mightier than what I fear and dread. I seek refuge in Allah, besides Whom none has the right to be worshipped, Who holds the seven heavens from falling upon the earth except by His permission, from the evil of Your servant so-and-so, and his troops, his followers and his supporters, from among the jinn and mankind. O Allah, be my protector against their evil. Glorious is Your praise, mighty is the one under Your protection, blessed is Your name, and there is no god other than You.
krb11.narr: Abdullah ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), as his own statement (mawquf)
krb11.note: When going to a formidable ruler whose assault you fear; mention the person’s name in place of “so-and-so”

krb12.t: O Allah, Revealer of the Book, Swift in reckoning, defeat the confederates. O Allah, defeat them and shake them.
krb12.narr: Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa (may Allah be pleased with them both)
krb12.note: The Prophet ﷺ supplicated with it against the confederates (al-Ahzab)

krb13.t: O Allah, suffice me against them however You will.
krb13.narr: Suhayb al-Rumi (may Allah be pleased with him)
krb13.note: The believing boy in the story of the People of the Ditch said it when they tried to kill him, and Allah protected him from them

krb14.t: O Allah, suffice me with what You have made lawful against what You have made unlawful, and by Your bounty make me independent of all besides You.
krb14.narr: Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him)
krb14.fadl: “Shall I not teach you words that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught me? Even if you had a debt like Mount Sir, Allah would settle it for you.”

krb15.t: O Allah, nothing is easy except what You make easy, and You make the difficult, if You will, easy.
krb15.narr: Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him)

krb16.t: It is the decree of Allah, and He does what He wills.
krb16.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
krb16.fadl: “If something befalls you, do not say: ‘If only I had done such-and-such, it would have been such-and-such.’ Rather say: ‘It is the decree of Allah, and He does what He wills,’ for ‘if only’ opens the door to the work of Satan.”

hsn01.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hsn01.fadl: “Satan comes to one of you and says: Who created this? Who created that? — until he says: Who created your Lord? When he reaches that, let him seek refuge in Allah and stop [such thoughts].”
hsn01.note: Seek refuge in Allah and stop pursuing the whisper

hsn02.t: I believe in Allah and His messengers.
hsn02.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hsn02.fadl: “People will keep asking questions until it is said: Allah created creation, so who created Allah? Whoever finds any of that, let him say: I believe in Allah.” Another narration adds: “and His messengers.”

hsn03.t: He is the First and the Last, the Ascendant and the Intimate, and He is, of all things, Knowing.
hsn03.narr: 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both)
hsn03.fadl: “If you find something [of doubt] in yourself, say: ‘He is the First and the Last, the Ascendant and the Intimate, and He is, of all things, Knowing.’”

hsn04.t: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the outcast.
hsn04.narr: 'Uthman ibn Abi al-'As (may Allah be pleased with him)
hsn04.fadl: “That is a devil called Khinzab. When you sense him, seek refuge in Allah from him and spit lightly to your left three times.” He said: I did that and Allah took him away from me.
hsn04.note: For distraction in prayer and recitation: seek refuge and spit lightly (dry spitting) to the left three times

hsn05.t: I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from Satan the outcast — from his madness, his arrogance and his poetry.
hsn05.narr: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him)
hsn05.note: Seeking refuge repels Satan; the Prophet ﷺ said this when opening the night prayer. Allah says: “And say: My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the incitements of the devils” (23:97)

hsn06.t: When the call to prayer is made, Satan turns his back and flees, passing wind, so that he does not hear the call.
hsn06.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hsn06.note: The adhan drives Satan away — a hadith to know and act upon

hsn07.t: Do not make your houses graveyards. Satan flees from the house in which Surat al-Baqarah is recited.
hsn07.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hsn07.note: Remembrance and Quran recitation drive Satan away: e.g. the morning and evening adhkar, adhkar of sleeping and waking, entering and leaving the home and mosque, and Ayat al-Kursi and the end of al-Baqarah before sleep

hsn08.t: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah, which no righteous or wicked person can exceed, from the evil of what He has created, made and brought into being; from the evil of what descends from the sky and the evil of what ascends to it; from the evil of what He has spread on the earth and the evil of what comes out of it; from the evil of the trials of the night and the day; and from the evil of every night visitor, except a visitor who comes with good, O Most Merciful.
hsn08.narr: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Khanbash (may Allah be pleased with him)
hsn08.note: Jibril taught it to the Prophet ﷺ on the night the devils plotted against him; when he said it, Allah extinguished their fire and defeated them

hsn09.narr: Abu al-Darda' (may Allah be pleased with him)
hsn09.fadl: “Whoever memorizes ten verses from the beginning of Surat al-Kahf will be protected from the Dajjal.”
hsn09.note: The first ten verses of Surat al-Kahf; in another narration of Muslim: “from the end of al-Kahf”

hsn10.t: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave, from the punishment of Hell, from the trials of life and death, and from the evil of the trial of the False Messiah (al-Dajjal).
hsn10.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hsn10.note: Said after the final tashahhud, before the taslim, in every prayer

hsn11.t: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from associating partners with You knowingly, and I seek Your forgiveness for what I do not know.
hsn11.narr: Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (may Allah be pleased with him)
hsn11.note: Supplication for fear of shirk; in al-Adab al-Mufrad it is from Ma'qil ibn Yasar about Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with them)

hsn12.t: O Allah, there is no omen except Your decree, there is no good except Your good, and there is no god other than You.
hsn12.narr: 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr (may Allah be pleased with them both)
hsn12.fadl: “Whoever is turned back from his need by an evil omen has committed shirk.” They asked: What is the expiation for that? He said: “That one of them says: O Allah, there is no good except Your good, no omen except Your decree, and there is no god other than You.”
hsn12.note: Said by one who feels a bad omen; as for good optimism (fa'l), the Prophet ﷺ liked it

hsn13.t: None has the right to be worshipped except Allah.
hsn13.narr: Zaynab bint Jahsh (may Allah be pleased with her)
hsn13.fadl: The Prophet ﷺ came in to her in a state of fright, saying: “None has the right to be worshipped except Allah; woe to the Arabs from an evil that has drawn near.”

mrd01.t: No harm; (it is) a purification, if Allah wills.
mrd01.narr: Abdullah ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both)
mrd01.note: The Prophet ﷺ said this whenever he visited a sick person

mrd02.t: I ask Allah the Magnificent, Lord of the Magnificent Throne, to cure you.
mrd02.narr: Abdullah ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both)
mrd02.fadl: “Whoever visits a sick person whose appointed time has not come and says seven times in his presence: ‘I ask Allah the Magnificent, Lord of the Magnificent Throne, to cure you,’ Allah will cure him of that illness.”

mrd03.t: When a man visits his (sick) Muslim brother, he walks among the harvest of Paradise until he sits down, and when he sits, mercy envelops him. If it is in the morning, seventy thousand angels pray for him until the evening, and if it is in the evening, seventy thousand angels pray for him until the morning.
mrd03.narr: Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him)
mrd03.note: A hadith on the virtue of visiting the sick, not a dhikr to be recited

mrd04.t: O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, and join me with the highest companionship.
mrd04.narr: Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her)
mrd04.note: Said by the Prophet ﷺ in his final illness while leaning against Aishah

mrd05.t: None has the right to be worshipped except Allah; indeed, death has its agonies.
mrd05.narr: Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her)
mrd05.note: At the time of his death, the Prophet ﷺ would put his hands in water, wipe his face with them and say this

mrd06.t: None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, and Allah is the greatest. None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, alone. None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, alone, without partner. None has the right to be worshipped except Allah; to Him belongs all sovereignty and all praise. None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, and there is no might nor power except with Allah.
mrd06.narr: Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri and Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with them both)
mrd06.fadl: “Whoever says them during his illness and then dies, the Fire will not consume him.”

mrd07.narr: ‘Uthman ibn Abi al-‘As al-Thaqafi (may Allah be pleased with him)
mrd07.note: Place your hand on the part of the body that hurts and say “Bismillah” three times, then “I seek refuge in Allah and His power…” seven times

mrd08.t: I seek refuge in Allah and His power from the evil of what I feel and what I fear.
mrd08.narr: ‘Uthman ibn Abi al-‘As al-Thaqafi (may Allah be pleased with him)
mrd08.note: Place your hand on the part of the body that hurts and say “Bismillah” three times, then “I seek refuge in Allah and His power…” seven times

mrd09.t: If one of you sees something of his brother, of himself or of his wealth that pleases him, let him supplicate for blessing (barakah) for it, for the evil eye is real.
mrd09.narr: ‘Amir ibn Rabi‘ah and Sahl ibn Hunayf (may Allah be pleased with them both), via Abu Umamah ibn Sahl
mrd09.note: Prophetic guidance: whoever fears afflicting something with the evil eye should ask Allah to bless it

mrd10.t: I commend you both to the protection of Allah’s perfect words from every devil and every poisonous creature, and from every harmful eye.
mrd10.narr: Abdullah ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both)
mrd10.fadl: “Your father (Ibrahim) used to seek protection with these for Isma‘il and Ishaq.”
mrd10.note: The Prophet ﷺ used it for al-Hasan and al-Husayn; adjust the pronoun to the number of children

hom01.t: In the name of Allah, I place my trust in Allah, and there is no might nor power except with Allah.
hom01.narr: Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him)
hom01.fadl: “It is said to him then: You have been guided, sufficed and protected; and the devils move away from him.”

hom02.t: O Allah, I seek refuge in You lest I go astray or be led astray, lest I slip or be made to slip, lest I wrong others or be wronged, lest I behave foolishly or be treated foolishly.
hom02.narr: Umm Salamah (may Allah be pleased with her)
hom02.note: When the Prophet ﷺ left his house, he would raise his gaze to the sky and say it

hom03.t: In the name of Allah we enter, in the name of Allah we leave, and upon Allah our Lord we place our trust.
hom03.narr: Abu Malik al-Ash'ari (may Allah be pleased with him)
hom03.note: Then greet your family with salam. Ibn Baz graded its chain hasan (Tuhfat al-Akhyar), while al-Albani graded it weak due to a break in the chain. Established in Sahih Muslim (2018): “When a man enters his house and mentions Allah on entering and when eating, the devil says: No lodging for you and no dinner.”

hom04.t: In the name of Allah. O Allah, I seek refuge with You from evil and evil ones (the male and female devils).
hom04.narr: Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him)
hom04.note: Said before entering. The basmalah at the beginning is narrated by Sa'id ibn Mansur, as cited in Fath al-Bari, and is supported by Ali's hadith in al-Tirmidhi (606)

hom05.narr: Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her)

hom06.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
hom06.fadl: “There is no ablution for the one who does not mention the name of Allah over it.”

hom07.t: I bear witness that none has the right to be worshipped except Allah alone, without partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.
hom07.narr: Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him)
hom07.fadl: “None of you performs ablution thoroughly and then says: … except that the eight gates of Paradise are opened for him, and he may enter by whichever he wishes.”

hom08.t: O Allah, make me among those who repent often and make me among those who purify themselves.
hom08.narr: Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him)
hom08.note: Said after the two testimonies following ablution

hom09.t: How perfect You are, O Allah, and with Your praise. I bear witness that none has the right to be worshipped except You. I seek Your forgiveness and turn to You in repentance.
hom09.narr: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him)
hom09.fadl: “… it will be written on a parchment and sealed with a seal that will not be broken until the Day of Resurrection.”
hom09.note: After ablution. It is narrated both from the Prophet ﷺ and as Abu Sa'id's own words; al-Albani graded it sahih, the latter having the ruling of a prophetic report

lbs01.t: All praise is for Allah who has clothed me with this garment and provided it for me, without any might or power on my part.
lbs01.narr: Mu'adh ibn Anas al-Juhani (may Allah be pleased with him)
lbs01.fadl: “… his past sins will be forgiven.”

lbs02.t: O Allah, to You belongs all praise. You have clothed me with it. I ask You for its good and the good for which it was made, and I seek refuge with You from its evil and the evil for which it was made.
lbs02.narr: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him)
lbs02.note: When the Prophet ﷺ put on a new garment, he would name it — a turban, a shirt or a cloak — and then say this

lbs03.t: May you wear it out, and may Allah the Exalted replace it (with another).
lbs03.narr: The Companions of the Prophet ﷺ (reported by Abu Nadrah)
lbs03.note: When one of the Companions put on a new garment, this was said to him; it is a supplication for long life

lbs04.t: Wear new clothes, live a praiseworthy life, and die a martyr.
lbs04.narr: Abdullah ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with him)
lbs04.note: The Prophet ﷺ said it to Umar when he saw him wearing a shirt

lbs05.narr: Ali ibn Abi Talib and Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with them)
lbs05.fadl: “The screen between the eyes of the jinn and the private parts of the children of Adam, when one of them enters the toilet, is that he says: In the name of Allah.”
lbs05.note: When undressing. Al-Tabarani's wording in al-Awsat from Anas has: “when one of them takes off his garment”; al-Albani graded it sahih (Sahih al-Jami')

ftm01.narr: Umar ibn Abi Salamah and Aishah (may Allah be pleased with them)
ftm01.fadl: “O boy, mention the name of Allah, eat with your right hand, and eat from what is in front of you.”

ftm02.t: In the name of Allah at its beginning and its end.
ftm02.narr: Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her)
ftm02.fadl: “When one of you eats, let him say: In the name of Allah. If he forgets at the beginning, let him say: In the name of Allah at its beginning and its end.”
ftm02.note: If you forgot to say Bismillah at the start of the meal

ftm03.t: O Allah, bless it for us and feed us better than it.
ftm03.narr: Abdullah ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him)
ftm03.note: For whoever Allah has given food

ftm04.t: O Allah, bless it for us and give us more of it.
ftm04.narr: Abdullah ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him)
ftm04.note: For whoever Allah has given milk to drink

ftm05.t: All praise is for Allah who has fed me this and provided it for me, without any might or power on my part.
ftm05.narr: Mu'adh ibn Anas al-Juhani (may Allah be pleased with him)
ftm05.fadl: “… his past sins will be forgiven.”

ftm06.t: All praise is for Allah, abundant, good and blessed praise; praise that is never enough, never abandoned, and never dispensed with, our Lord.
ftm06.narr: Abu Umamah al-Bahili (may Allah be pleased with him)
ftm06.note: The Prophet ﷺ would say it when his table was cleared away

ftm07.t: O Allah, bless them in what You have provided them, forgive them and have mercy on them.
ftm07.narr: Abdullah ibn Busr (may Allah be pleased with him)
ftm07.note: The guest's supplication for the host

ftm08.t: O Allah, feed the one who fed me, and give drink to the one who gave me drink.
ftm08.narr: al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad (may Allah be pleased with him)

ftm09.t: O Allah, bless our fruit for us, bless our city for us, bless our sa' for us, and bless our mudd for us.
ftm09.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
ftm09.note: On seeing the first fruit of the season; then give it to the youngest child present. The sa' and the mudd are measures of volume

sfr01.t: In the name of Allah, and all praise is for Allah. How perfect He is, the One Who has placed this (transport) at our service, and we ourselves would not have been capable of that, and to our Lord is our final return. All praise is for Allah, all praise is for Allah, all praise is for Allah. Allah is the greatest, Allah is the greatest, Allah is the greatest. How perfect You are, O Allah; verily I have wronged my soul, so forgive me, for surely none forgives sins except You.
sfr01.narr: Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him)
sfr01.fadl: “Indeed your Lord is pleased with His servant when he says: ‘Forgive me my sins’ — (Allah says:) he knows that none forgives sins but Me.”
sfr01.note: Say “Bismillah” when putting your foot in the stirrup (or getting in), “al-hamdu lillah” once seated, then complete the rest

sfr02.t: Allah is the greatest, Allah is the greatest, Allah is the greatest. How perfect He is, the One Who has placed this (transport) at our service, and we ourselves would not have been capable of that, and to our Lord is our final return. O Allah, we ask You on this journey of ours for righteousness (birr) and piety (taqwa), and for deeds which please You. O Allah, make this journey of ours easy for us and shorten its distance for us. O Allah, You are the Companion on the journey and the Successor (guardian) over the family. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the hardships of travel, from a distressing sight, and from an evil outcome in wealth and family.
sfr02.narr: Abdullah ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both)
sfr02.note: The Prophet ﷺ said it when mounted and setting out on a journey. On returning he said the same and added: “We return, repenting, worshipping, and praising our Lord.”

sfr03.t: O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and all that they shade, Lord of the seven earths and all that they carry, Lord of the devils and all whom they misguide, Lord of the winds and all that they scatter. I ask You for the good of this town, the good of its people and the good of what is in it, and I seek refuge in You from its evil, the evil of its people and the evil of what is in it.
sfr03.narr: Suhayb al-Rumi (may Allah be pleased with him)
sfr03.note: Said on seeing the town or city you intend to enter

sfr04.t: None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, alone, without partner. To Him belongs all sovereignty and all praise. He gives life and causes death, and He is Ever-Living and does not die. In His hand is all good, and He is over all things competent.
sfr04.narr: Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him)
sfr04.fadl: “Whoever enters the market and says: … Allah records for him a million good deeds, erases from him a million bad deeds, and raises him a million degrees.”

sfr05.narr: A Companion who was riding behind the Prophet ﷺ (may Allah be pleased with him)
sfr05.fadl: “Do not say: ‘May the devil perish,’ for if you say that he swells until he is like a house and says: ‘By my power.’ Rather say: ‘Bismillah,’ for if you say that he shrinks until he is like a fly.”

sfr06.t: I entrust you to Allah, Whose trusts are never lost.
sfr06.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
sfr06.note: Said by the traveller to those he leaves behind. Ibn Majah’s wording addresses one person: “astawdi‘uka Allah…” (I entrust you [singular] …)

sfr07.t: I entrust to Allah your religion, your trustworthiness, and the final outcomes of your deeds.
sfr07.narr: Abdullah ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both)
sfr07.note: Said by the one staying behind when bidding farewell to a traveller

sfr08.t: May Allah provide you with taqwa (piety), forgive your sins, and make good easy for you wherever you are.
sfr08.narr: Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him)
sfr08.note: The Prophet ﷺ said it to a man who told him: “I intend to travel, so give me provision (advice).”

sfr09.narr: Jabir ibn Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with them both)
sfr09.note: When going uphill on a journey. Jabir said: “When we went up (a height) we would say Allahu akbar, and when we went down we would say subhan Allah.”

sfr10.t: How perfect Allah is (Glory be to Allah).
sfr10.narr: Jabir ibn Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with them both)
sfr10.note: When going downhill on a journey. Jabir said: “When we went up (a height) we would say Allahu akbar, and when we went down we would say subhan Allah.”

sfr11.t: May a listener (bear witness and) make known our praise of Allah and His excellent favours upon us. Our Lord, be our Companion (and protect us) and bestow Your bounty upon us — seeking refuge in Allah from the Fire.
sfr11.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
sfr11.note: The Prophet ﷺ said it when travelling at the time of sahar (the last part of the night, just before dawn)

sfr12.t: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created.
sfr12.narr: Khawlah bint Hakim al-Sulamiyyah (may Allah be pleased with her)
sfr12.fadl: “Whoever stops at a place and says: ‘I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created,’ nothing will harm him until he departs from that place.”
sfr12.note: When stopping at a place, on a journey or otherwise

sfr13.t: Allah is the greatest, Allah is the greatest, Allah is the greatest. None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, alone, without partner. To Him belongs all sovereignty and all praise, and He is over all things competent. We return, repenting, worshipping, and praising our Lord. Allah fulfilled His promise, aided His servant, and alone defeated the confederates.
sfr13.narr: Abdullah ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both)
sfr13.note: On returning from a journey: say Allahu akbar three times at every elevated place, then say the rest

mtr01.t: O Allah, I ask You for its good, and I seek refuge in You from its evil.
mtr01.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
mtr01.fadl: “The wind is from the mercy (rawh) of Allah; it brings mercy and it brings punishment. When you see it, do not curse it, but ask Allah for its good and seek refuge in Allah from its evil.”

mtr02.t: O Allah, I ask You for its good, the good within it and the good it was sent with, and I seek refuge in You from its evil, the evil within it and the evil it was sent with.
mtr02.narr: Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her)
mtr02.note: The Prophet ﷺ said it when the wind blew strongly

mtr03.t: How perfect is He Whom the thunder glorifies with His praise, as do the angels out of fear of Him.
mtr03.narr: Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr (may Allah be pleased with them both), from his practice (mawquf)
mtr03.note: When he heard thunder, he would stop talking and say this

mtr04.t: O Allah, give us rain that relieves, that is wholesome and fertile, beneficial and not harmful, soon and not delayed.
mtr04.narr: Jabir ibn Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with them both)

mtr05.t: O Allah, send us rain; O Allah, send us rain; O Allah, send us rain.
mtr05.narr: Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him)
mtr05.note: The Prophet ﷺ said it with raised hands during the Friday sermon when drought was complained of

mtr06.t: O Allah, give water to Your servants and Your livestock, spread Your mercy, and revive Your dead land.
mtr06.narr: Abdullah ibn ‘Amr ibn al-‘As (may Allah be pleased with them both)
mtr06.note: The Prophet ﷺ said it when praying for rain

mtr07.t: O Allah, (make it) a beneficial downpour.
mtr07.narr: Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her)
mtr07.note: The Prophet ﷺ said it when he saw rain

mtr08.t: We have been given rain by the grace and mercy of Allah.
mtr08.narr: Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani (may Allah be pleased with him)
mtr08.fadl: Allah said: “This morning some of My servants became believers in Me and some disbelievers. As for the one who said: ‘We have been given rain by the grace and mercy of Allah,’ he is a believer in Me and a disbeliever in the stars.”

mtr09.t: O Allah, (let it fall) around us and not upon us. O Allah, (let it fall) on the hillocks and the high ground, the valley beds, and the places where trees grow.
mtr09.narr: Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him)
mtr09.note: When rain becomes excessive and harm is feared

haj01.t: Here I am, O Allah, here I am. Here I am, You have no partner, here I am. Verily all praise and blessings are Yours, and all sovereignty. You have no partner.
haj01.narr: Abdullah ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both)
haj01.note: The Talbiyah of the pilgrim in ihram for Hajj or ‘Umrah; men raise their voices with it

haj02.narr: Abdullah ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both)
haj02.note: The Prophet ﷺ circled the Ka‘bah on a camel; every time he came to the Corner (the Black Stone) he pointed to it with something he held and said Allahu akbar

haj03.t: Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.
haj03.narr: Abdullah ibn al-Sa’ib (may Allah be pleased with him)
haj03.note: Between the Yemeni Corner and the Black Stone during tawaf (al-Baqarah 2:201)

haj04.t: Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah. I begin with what Allah began with.
haj04.narr: Jabir ibn Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with them both)
haj04.note: When the Prophet ﷺ drew near to al-Safa he recited the verse (al-Baqarah 2:158) and said: “I begin with what Allah began with,” and began with al-Safa

haj05.t: None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, alone, without partner. To Him belongs all sovereignty and all praise, and He is over all things competent. None has the right to be worshipped except Allah alone; He fulfilled His promise, aided His servant, and alone defeated the confederates.
haj05.narr: Jabir ibn Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with them both)
haj05.note: On al-Safa, and likewise on al-Marwah: climb until the Ka‘bah is visible, face the qiblah, declare Allah’s oneness and greatness (Allahu akbar), and say this three times, supplicating in between

haj06.t: None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, alone, without partner. To Him belongs all sovereignty and all praise, and He is over all things competent.
haj06.narr: Abdullah ibn ‘Amr ibn al-‘As (may Allah be pleased with them both)
haj06.fadl: “The best supplication is the supplication on the Day of ‘Arafah, and the best of what I and the prophets before me have said is: ‘None has the right to be worshipped except Allah, alone, without partner…’”

haj07.t: Allah is the greatest; none has the right to be worshipped except Allah.
haj07.narr: Jabir ibn Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with them both)
haj07.fadl: “The Prophet ﷺ rode al-Qaswa’ until he reached al-Mash‘ar al-Haram. He faced the qiblah and supplicated to Allah, declared His greatness (takbir), said La ilaha illallah (tahlil) and declared His oneness, and remained standing until the sky was very bright; then he moved on before sunrise.”
haj07.note: At al-Mash‘ar al-Haram in Muzdalifah after Fajr: face the qiblah and keep supplicating, saying Allahu akbar and La ilaha illallah, until it is very bright

haj08.narr: Abdullah ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both)
haj08.note: Say Allahu akbar with each pebble at the three Jamarat. After the first and second, step forward, stand facing the qiblah with raised hands and supplicate. At Jamrat al-‘Aqabah, throw, saying Allahu akbar with each pebble, then leave without standing there

ist01.t: O Allah, I seek Your guidance (in choosing) by Your knowledge, and I seek ability by Your power, and I ask You of Your immense bounty; for You are able and I am not, You know and I do not, and You are the Knower of the unseen. O Allah, if You know that this matter is good for me in my religion, my livelihood and the outcome of my affairs, then decree it for me, make it easy for me, then bless me in it. And if You know that this matter is bad for me in my religion, my livelihood and the outcome of my affairs, then turn it away from me and turn me away from it, and decree for me what is good wherever it may be, then make me content with it.
ist01.narr: Jabir ibn Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with them both)
ist01.fadl: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to teach us istikharah in all matters, just as he taught us a surah of the Quran. He would say: ‘When one of you intends to do something, let him pray two rak‘ahs other than the obligatory prayer, then say: …’”
ist01.note: Pray two voluntary rak‘ahs, then make this supplication, naming your need at “this matter”. In both places the narrator was unsure whether he said “and the outcome of my affairs” or “in my immediate and later affairs”. One who seeks the Creator’s guidance, consults the believers and is careful in his affair will not regret it; Allah says: “And consult them in the matter; then when you have decided, put your trust in Allah” (Al ‘Imran 3:159)

ist02.t: O Allah, guide me among those You have guided, grant me well-being among those You have granted well-being, take me into Your care among those You have taken into Your care, bless me in what You have given, and protect me from the evil of what You have decreed; for You decree and none can decree over You. Indeed, the one You befriend is never humiliated, and the one You take as an enemy is never honoured. Blessed are You, our Lord, and Exalted.
ist02.narr: al-Hasan ibn ‘Ali (may Allah be pleased with them both)
ist02.note: In the qunut of Witr; the Prophet ﷺ taught it to al-Hasan ibn ‘Ali. The phrase “the one You take as an enemy is never honoured” is in Abu Dawud’s narration

ist03.t: O Allah, I seek refuge in Your pleasure from Your anger, and in Your pardon from Your punishment, and I seek refuge in You from You. I cannot enumerate Your praise; You are as You have praised Yourself.
ist03.narr: Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him)
ist03.note: The Prophet ﷺ used to say it at the end of his Witr

ist04.t: O Allah, You alone we worship, to You we pray and prostrate, and towards You we strive and hasten. We hope for Your mercy and fear Your punishment; indeed Your punishment will overtake the disbelievers. O Allah, we seek Your help and Your forgiveness, we praise You with all good and do not deny You; we believe in You, submit to You, and disown whoever disbelieves in You.
ist04.narr: Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), from his practice (mawquf)
ist04.note: From the qunut of Umar ibn al-Khattab; al-Albani graded its chain sahih as Umar’s practice (Irwa’ al-Ghalil 2/170)

jnz01.t: None has the right to be worshipped except Allah.
jnz01.narr: Mu‘adh ibn Jabal (may Allah be pleased with him)
jnz01.fadl: “Whoever’s last words are ‘La ilaha illallah’ will enter Paradise.”
jnz01.note: Gently prompt the dying person to say it. In Sahih Muslim (916): “Prompt your dying ones to say La ilaha illallah.”

jnz02.t: To Allah we belong and to Him we shall return. O Allah, reward me in my affliction and replace it for me with something better.
jnz02.narr: Umm Salamah (may Allah be pleased with her)
jnz02.fadl: “No Muslim is struck by a calamity and says what Allah has commanded: ‘To Allah we belong and to Him we shall return; O Allah, reward me in my affliction and replace it for me with something better,’ except that Allah replaces it for him with something better.”

jnz03.t: O Allah, forgive so-and-so, raise his rank among the rightly guided, be a successor (guardian) for those he leaves behind, and forgive us and him, O Lord of the worlds. Make his grave spacious for him and illuminate it for him.
jnz03.narr: Umm Salamah (may Allah be pleased with her)
jnz03.note: Mention the deceased by name in place of “so-and-so”. The Prophet ﷺ said it for Abu Salamah after closing his eyes

jnz04.t: O Allah, forgive him and have mercy on him, keep him safe and pardon him. Honour his reception and make his entrance wide. Wash him with water, snow and hail, and cleanse him of sins as You cleanse a white garment of dirt. Give him a home better than his home, a family better than his family, and a spouse better than his spouse. Admit him into Paradise, and protect him from the punishment of the grave and the punishment of the Fire.
jnz04.narr: ‘Awf ibn Malik al-Ashja‘i (may Allah be pleased with him)
jnz04.fadl: ‘Awf said: “…until I wished that I were that deceased person.”
jnz04.note: In the funeral prayer. In Muslim’s narration: “from the punishment of the grave — or from the punishment of the Fire —”

jnz05.t: O Allah, forgive our living and our dead, those present and those absent, our young and our old, our males and our females. O Allah, whomever of us You keep alive, keep him alive upon Islam, and whomever of us You take, take him upon faith. O Allah, do not deprive us of his reward, and do not let us go astray after him.
jnz05.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)

jnz06.t: O Allah, so-and-so son of so-and-so is in Your care and under Your protection, so protect him from the trial of the grave and the punishment of the Fire. You are the One Who fulfils promises and the Truth. So forgive him and have mercy on him; indeed You are the Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful.
jnz06.narr: Wathilah ibn al-Asqa‘ (may Allah be pleased with him)
jnz06.note: In the funeral prayer; mention the deceased in place of “so-and-so son of so-and-so”

jnz07.t: O Allah, Your servant, the son of Your maidservant, is in need of Your mercy, and You have no need to punish him. If he did good, then increase his good deeds, and if he did wrong, then overlook his wrongs.
jnz07.narr: Yazid ibn Rukanah (may Allah be pleased with him)
jnz07.note: In the funeral prayer. Graded sahih by al-Hakim, with al-Dhahabi agreeing; see al-Albani, Ahkam al-Jana’iz p. 125

jnz08.t: O Allah, protect him from the punishment of the grave.
jnz08.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), from his practice when praying over a child
jnz08.note: In the funeral prayer for a child. It is also good to say what the scholars mention (see Ibn Qudamah’s al-Mughni 3/416 and Ibn Baz): “O Allah, make him a forerunner and a stored treasure for his parents, and an intercessor whose intercession is accepted. O Allah, through him make their scales heavy and their reward great. Join him with the righteous believers, place him in the care of Ibrahim, and by Your mercy protect him from the punishment of Hellfire. Give him a home better than his home and a family better than his family. O Allah, forgive those who preceded us, our little ones who died before us, and those who preceded us in faith.”

jnz09.t: O Allah, make him for us a forerunner, one who has gone ahead, and a (source of) reward.
jnz09.narr: al-Hasan al-Basri (may Allah have mercy on him), from his practice
jnz09.note: Al-Hasan would recite al-Fatihah over a child and say this. Al-Bukhari reports it without a chain (mu‘allaq) in the Book of Funerals, chapter on reciting al-Fatihah in the funeral prayer (before hadith 1335); ‘Abd al-Razzaq reports it with a chain

jnz10.t: Verily to Allah belongs what He took, and to Him belongs what He gave, and everything with Him has an appointed term; so let her be patient and hope for (Allah’s) reward.
jnz10.narr: Usamah ibn Zayd (may Allah be pleased with them both)
jnz10.note: The Prophet ﷺ sent this message to his daughter when her son was dying; adjust “let her be patient…” to the person addressed. It is also good to say: “May Allah make your reward great, grant you good solace, and forgive your deceased” (mentioned by al-Nawawi in al-Adhkar; not a hadith of the Prophet ﷺ)

jnz11.t: In the name of Allah, and according to the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah.
jnz11.narr: Abdullah ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both)
jnz11.note: When placing the deceased in the grave

jnz12.t: O Allah, forgive him. O Allah, make him steadfast.
jnz12.narr: ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan (may Allah be pleased with him)
jnz12.fadl: When the Prophet ﷺ finished burying the dead, he would stand by the grave and say: “Seek forgiveness for your brother and ask that he be made steadfast, for he is now being questioned.”

jnz13.t: Peace be upon you, O inhabitants of these dwellings, from among the believers and the Muslims. We shall, if Allah wills, join you. May Allah have mercy on those of us who have gone ahead and those who come later. I ask Allah for well-being for us and for you.
jnz13.narr: Buraydah ibn al-Husayb and Aishah (may Allah be pleased with them both)
jnz13.note: When visiting graves. The phrase “May Allah have mercy on those of us who have gone ahead…” is from Aishah’s hadith (Muslim 974)

dly01.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
dly01.fadl: “When one of you sneezes, let him say: All praise is for Allah. And let his brother or companion say to him: May Allah have mercy on you. When he says to him ‘May Allah have mercy on you,’ let him say: May Allah guide you and set your affairs right.”
dly01.note: Said by the one who sneezes

dly02.t: May Allah have mercy on you.
dly02.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
dly02.fadl: “When one of you sneezes, let him say: All praise is for Allah. And let his brother or companion say to him: May Allah have mercy on you. When he says to him ‘May Allah have mercy on you,’ let him say: May Allah guide you and set your affairs right.”
dly02.note: Said by the one who hears the sneezer praise Allah

dly03.t: May Allah guide you and set your affairs right.
dly03.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
dly03.fadl: “When one of you sneezes, let him say: All praise is for Allah. And let his brother or companion say to him: May Allah have mercy on you. When he says to him ‘May Allah have mercy on you,’ let him say: May Allah guide you and set your affairs right.”
dly03.note: The sneezer's reply to the one who said “May Allah have mercy on you”

dly04.t: May Allah guide you and set your affairs right.
dly04.narr: Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (may Allah be pleased with him)
dly04.fadl: The Jews used to sneeze in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ hoping he would say to them “May Allah have mercy on you,” but he would say: “May Allah guide you and set your affairs right.”
dly04.note: Said to a non-Muslim who sneezes and praises Allah

dly05.t: May Allah bless [your spouse] for you, and bless you, and bring you both together in goodness.
dly05.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
dly05.note: Said to congratulate someone who has married

dly06.t: O Allah, I ask You for her good and the good of the nature You have created her with, and I seek refuge in You from her evil and the evil of the nature You have created her with.
dly06.narr: 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr (may Allah be pleased with them both)
dly06.fadl: “When one of you marries a woman or acquires a servant, let him say: … And when he buys a camel, let him take hold of the top of its hump and say the same.”
dly06.note: Said by the groom on the wedding night, and likewise when buying a riding animal

dly07.t: In the name of Allah. O Allah, keep Satan away from us and keep Satan away from what You provide us with.
dly07.narr: 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both)
dly07.fadl: “For if a child is decreed for them from that [union], Satan will never harm it.”
dly07.note: Said before intimacy with one's spouse

dly08.t: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the outcast.
dly08.narr: Sulayman ibn Surad (may Allah be pleased with him)
dly08.fadl: “I know a word which, if he said it, what he feels would leave him: if he said, I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the outcast.”

dly09.t: All praise is for Allah who has spared me from what He has afflicted you with, and has favoured me greatly over much of what He has created.
dly09.narr: Abu Hurayrah and 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with them)
dly09.fadl: “Whoever sees someone afflicted and says: All praise is for Allah who has spared me from what He has afflicted you with and has favoured me greatly over much of what He has created — that affliction will not befall him.”
dly09.note: Scholars said: say it quietly so the afflicted person does not hear it and is not hurt

dly10.t: My Lord, forgive me and accept my repentance; indeed You are the Accepter of repentance, the Most Forgiving.
dly10.narr: 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both)
dly10.fadl: It would be counted that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said in a single sitting, a hundred times before getting up: “My Lord, forgive me and accept my repentance; indeed You are the Accepter of repentance, the Most Forgiving.”
dly10.note: The wording is al-Tirmidhi's; Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah have “the Accepter of repentance, the Most Merciful”

dly11.t: Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You. I bear witness that none has the right to be worshipped except You. I seek Your forgiveness and turn to You in repentance.
dly11.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
dly11.fadl: “Whoever sits in a gathering in which there is much idle talk, and before getting up says: Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You; I bear witness that none has the right to be worshipped except You; I seek Your forgiveness and turn to You in repentance — he will be forgiven what happened in that gathering.”
dly11.note: Expiation of the gathering: said before getting up from it

dly12.narr: 'Abdullah ibn Sarjis (may Allah be pleased with him)
dly12.fadl: I came to the Prophet ﷺ and ate of his food, then said: May Allah forgive you, O Messenger of Allah. He said: “And you.”
dly12.note: Said to someone who says “May Allah forgive you.” The story is in Ahmad; its basis is in Muslim with the wording: Did the Prophet ﷺ ask forgiveness for you? He said: “Yes, and for you.”

dly13.t: May Allah reward you with good.
dly13.narr: Usamah ibn Zayd (may Allah be pleased with them both)
dly13.fadl: “Whoever has a favour done for him and says to the one who did it, ‘May Allah reward you with good,’ has done his utmost in praising him.”
dly13.note: Said to someone who does you a favour

dly14.t: May He for whose sake you love me, love you.
dly14.narr: Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him)
dly14.note: Said to someone who says: I love you for the sake of Allah

dly15.t: May Allah bless you in your family and your wealth.
dly15.narr: Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him)
dly15.note: Said to someone who offers you his wealth; 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf said it to Sa'd ibn al-Rabi' (may Allah be pleased with them)

dly16.t: May Allah bless you in your family and your wealth. The reward for a loan is only praise and repayment.
dly16.narr: 'Abdullah ibn Abi Rabi'ah (may Allah be pleased with him)
dly16.note: Said to the lender when repaying the loan

dly17.t: You will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another. Shall I not tell you of something which, if you do it, you will love one another? Spread the greeting of peace among yourselves.
dly17.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
dly17.note: A hadith on the virtue of spreading the greeting of peace — read it to act upon it

dly18.t: Three things — whoever combines them has combined faith: being just with others from yourself, offering the greeting of peace to everyone, and spending [in charity] when in need.
dly18.narr: 'Ammar ibn Yasir (may Allah be pleased with them both)
dly18.note: A statement of 'Ammar (mawquf), cited by al-Bukhari without chain in the chapter heading before hadith 28

dly19.t: A man asked the Prophet ﷺ: Which [deed in] Islam is best? He said: “That you feed [others] and give the greeting of peace to those you know and those you do not know.”
dly19.narr: 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr (may Allah be pleased with them both)
dly19.note: A hadith on the virtue of spreading the greeting of peace — read it to act upon it

dly20.t: Peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings.
dly20.narr: 'Imran ibn Husayn (may Allah be pleased with them both)
dly20.fadl: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: Peace be upon you. He said: “Ten.” Another came and said: Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah. He said: “Twenty.” Another came and said: Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. He said: “Thirty.”
dly20.note: The complete greeting of peace (not in Hisn al-Muslim)

dly21.narr: Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him)
dly21.fadl: “When the People of the Book greet you, say: And upon you.”
dly21.note: Reply to a non-Muslim who greets you

dly22.t: When you hear roosters crowing, ask Allah of His bounty, for they have seen an angel; and when you hear a donkey braying, seek refuge in Allah from Satan, for it has seen a devil.
dly22.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
dly22.note: On hearing a rooster: ask Allah of His bounty; on hearing a donkey: seek refuge in Allah from Satan

dly23.t: When you hear dogs barking and donkeys braying at night, seek refuge in Allah from them, for they see what you do not see.
dly23.narr: Jabir ibn 'Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with them both)
dly23.note: Seek refuge in Allah on hearing dogs barking at night

dly24.t: O Allah, any believer whom I have insulted, make that a means of drawing him near to You on the Day of Resurrection.
dly24.narr: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
dly24.note: The Prophet's ﷺ supplication for one he had spoken harshly to; Muslim's narration: “make it a purification and mercy for him”

dly25.t: I consider so-and-so to be — and Allah is his reckoner, and I do not vouch for anyone before Allah — I consider him to be such-and-such.
dly25.narr: Abu Bakrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
dly25.fadl: “If one of you must praise his companion, let him say: I consider so-and-so — and Allah is his reckoner, and I do not vouch for anyone before Allah — I consider him, if he knows that of him, to be such-and-such.”
dly25.note: Said when praising a fellow Muslim, if one knows that of him

dly26.t: O Allah, do not hold me accountable for what they say, forgive me for what they do not know, and make me better than what they think.
dly26.narr: 'Adi ibn Artah, from a man among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ
dly26.note: Said when one is praised; al-Albani authenticated its chain. The phrase “and make me better than what they think” is an addition from al-Bayhaqi's Shu'ab al-Iman via another route

dly27.t: All praise is for Allah, by whose favour good things are completed.
dly27.note: The Prophet ﷺ said it when something pleasing came to him

dly28.t: All praise is for Allah in every circumstance.
dly28.note: The Prophet ﷺ said it when something displeasing came to him

dly29.narr: Umm Salamah (may Allah be pleased with her)
dly29.fadl: The Prophet ﷺ woke one night and said: “Glory be to Allah! What trials have been sent down tonight, and what treasures have been opened!”

dly30.narr: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him)
dly30.fadl: “I hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise.” So we said: Allahu akbar.
dly30.note: Said when amazed or on hearing good news

dly31.t: When something pleasing came to the Prophet ﷺ, or he was given good news, he would fall down in prostration out of gratitude to Allah, Blessed and Exalted.
dly31.narr: Abu Bakrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
dly31.note: Prostration of gratitude upon receiving a blessing — a practice of the Prophet ﷺ

dly32.t: In the name of Allah, and Allah is the Greatest. O Allah, [it is] from You and for You. O Allah, accept [it] from me.
dly32.narr: Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him)
dly32.note: Said when slaughtering. “In the name of Allah, and Allah is the Greatest” is in Muslim from Anas; “O Allah, from You and for You” is in al-Bayhaqi and Abu Dawud from Jabir; “O Allah, accept from me” follows the meaning of Muslim's narration from 'A'ishah: “O Allah, accept from Muhammad and the family of Muhammad”

dly33.t: When night falls — or when evening comes — keep your children in, for the devils spread out at that time. When an hour of the night has passed, let them go. Close the doors and mention the name of Allah, for Satan does not open a closed door. Tie your waterskins and mention the name of Allah, and cover your vessels and mention the name of Allah, even if only by placing something across them, and put out your lamps.
dly33.narr: Jabir ibn 'Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with them both)
dly33.note: Comprehensive etiquette at nightfall — a hadith to know and act upon

books.bukhari_muallaq: Cited by al-Bukhari without a chain, before hadith
